n.21: Hebrew *resha'im*, plural of *rasha*: those who are guilty of wrong (see 2:22).

v: Wine is a mocker,[^1] beer[^2] a brawler, and whoever is led astray by it is not wise.
לֵ֣ץ הַ֭יַּ[t]ין הֹמֶ֣ה שֵׁכָ֑ר וְכָל־שֹׁ֥גֶה בּ֝֗וֹ לֹ֣א יֶחְכָּֽם׃
The terror of a king is like the roar of a lion; whoever provokes him forfeits his life.
נַ֣הַם כַּ֭כְּפִיר אֵ֣ימַת מֶ֑לֶךְ מִ֝תְעַבְּר֗וֹ חוֹטֵ֥א נַפְשֽׁוֹ׃
It is an honor for a person to keep away from strife, but every fool[^3] bursts into quarrels.
כָּב֣וֹד לָ֭אִישׁ שֶׁ֣בֶת מֵרִ֑יב וְכָל־אֱ֝וִ֗יל יִתְגַּלָּֽע׃
The lazy person[^4] does not plow in autumn; at harvest he looks for a crop, and there is nothing.
מֵ֭חֹרֶף עָצֵ֣ל לֹא־יַחֲרֹ֑שׁ *ישאל **וְשָׁאַ֖ל בַּקָּצִ֣יר וָאָֽיִן׃
The purpose in a person's heart is deep water, but a person of insight[^5] draws it out.
מַ֣יִם עֲ֭מֻקִּים עֵצָ֣ה בְלֶב־אִ֑ישׁ וְאִ֖ישׁ תְּבוּנָ֣ה יִדְלֶֽנָּה׃
Many a person proclaims his own loyalty,[^6] but a faithful person, who can find?
רָב־אָדָ֗ם יִ֭קְרָא אִ֣ישׁ חַסְדּ֑וֹ וְאִ֥ישׁ אֱ֝מוּנִ֗ים מִ֣י יִמְצָֽא׃
The righteous[^7] walks in his integrity; happy[^8] are his children after him.
מִתְהַלֵּ֣ךְ בְּתֻמּ֣וֹ צַדִּ֑יק אַשְׁרֵ֖י בָנָ֣יו אַחֲרָֽיו׃
A king who sits on the throne of judgment winnows out all evil with his eyes.
מֶ֗לֶךְ יוֹשֵׁ֥ב עַל־כִּסֵּא־דִ֑ין מְזָרֶ֖ה בְעֵינָ֣יו כָּל־רָֽע׃
Who can say, "I have made my heart clean; I am pure from my sin"?
מִֽי־יֹ֭אמַר זִכִּ֣יתִי לִבִּ֑י טָ֝הַ֗רְתִּי מֵחַטָּאתִֽי׃
Two different weights and two different measures,[^9] both are detestable to the LORD.[^10]
אֶ֣בֶן וָ֭אֶבֶן אֵיפָ֣ה וְאֵיפָ֑ה תּוֹעֲבַ֥ת יְ֝הוָ֗ה גַּם־שְׁנֵיהֶֽם׃
Even a child makes himself known by his actions,[^11] whether his conduct is pure and right.
גַּ֣ם בְּ֭מַעֲלָלָיו יִתְנַכֶּר־נָ֑עַר אִם־זַ֖ךְ וְאִם־יָשָׁ֣ר פָּעֳלֽוֹ׃
The ear that hears and the eye that sees, the LORD has made them both.
אֹ֣זֶן שֹׁ֭מַעַת וְעַ֣יִן רֹאָ֑ה יְ֝הוָ֗ה עָשָׂ֥ה גַם־שְׁנֵיהֶֽם׃
Do not love sleep, or you will become poor; open your eyes, and you will have plenty of bread.
אַל־תֶּֽאֱהַ֣ב שֵׁ֭נָה פֶּן־תִּוָּרֵ֑שׁ פְּקַ֖ח עֵינֶ֣יךָ שְֽׂבַֽע־לָֽחֶם׃
"Bad, bad," says the buyer; but when he goes on his way, then he boasts.
רַ֣ע רַ֭ע יֹאמַ֣ר הַקּוֹנֶ֑ה וְאֹזֵ֥ל ל֝֗וֹ אָ֣ז יִתְהַלָּֽל׃
There is gold and plenty of coral,[^12] but lips of knowledge are a precious jewel.
יֵ֣שׁ זָ֭הָב וְרָב־פְּנִינִ֑ים וּכְלִ֥י יְ֝קָ֗ר שִׂפְתֵי־דָֽעַת׃
Take the garment of one who puts up security for a stranger; hold it in pledge for a foreign woman.[^13]
לְֽקַח־בִּ֭גְדוֹ כִּי־עָ֣רַב זָ֑ר וּבְעַ֖ד *נכרים **נָכְרִיָּ֣ה חַבְלֵֽהוּ׃
Bread gained by deceit is sweet to a person, but afterward his mouth will be full of gravel.
עָרֵ֣ב לָ֭אִישׁ לֶ֣חֶם שָׁ֑קֶר וְ֝אַחַ֗ר יִמָּֽלֵא־פִ֥יהוּ חָצָֽץ׃
Plans are established by advice; wage war with guidance.[^14]
מַ֭חֲשָׁבוֹת בְּעֵצָ֣ה תִכּ֑וֹן וּ֝בְתַחְבֻּל֗וֹת עֲשֵׂ֣ה מִלְחָמָֽה׃
Whoever goes about as a gossip reveals secrets, so do not associate with one who talks too much.
גּֽוֹלֶה־סּ֭וֹד הוֹלֵ֣ךְ רָכִ֑יל וּלְפֹתֶ֥ה שְׂ֝פָתָ֗יו לֹ֣א תִתְעָרָֽב׃
Whoever curses his father or his mother, his lamp will go out in the blackest darkness.
מְ֭קַלֵּל אָבִ֣יו וְאִמּ֑וֹ יִֽדְעַ֥ךְ נֵ֝ר֗וֹ *באישון **בֶּאֱשׁ֥וּן חֹֽשֶׁךְ׃
An inheritance gained in haste at the beginning[^15] will not be blessed in the end.
נַ֭חֲלָה *מבחלת **מְבֹהֶ֣לֶת בָּרִאשֹׁנָ֑ה וְ֝אַחֲרִיתָ֗הּ לֹ֣א תְבֹרָֽךְ׃
Do not say, "I will pay back evil!" Wait for the LORD, and he will rescue you.
אַל־תֹּאמַ֥ר אֲשַׁלְּמָה־רָ֑ע קַוֵּ֥ה לַֽ֝יהוָ֗ה וְיֹ֣שַֽׁע לָֽךְ׃
Two different weights are detestable to the LORD, and dishonest scales are not good.
תּוֹעֲבַ֣ת יְ֭הוָה אֶ֣בֶן וָאָ֑בֶן וּמֹאזְנֵ֖י מִרְמָ֣ה לֹא־טֽוֹב׃
A man's steps are from the LORD; how then can anyone understand his own way?
מֵיהוָ֥ה מִצְעֲדֵי־גָ֑בֶר וְ֝אָדָ֗ם מַה־יָּבִ֥ין דַּרְכּֽוֹ׃
It is a trap for a person to say rashly, "It is holy!"[^16] and only afterward to think about his vows.
מוֹקֵ֣שׁ אָ֭דָם יָ֣לַע קֹ֑דֶשׁ וְאַחַ֖ר נְדָרִ֣ים לְבַקֵּֽר׃
A wise king winnows out the wicked[^17] and drives the wheel over them.[^18]
מְזָרֶ֣ה רְ֭שָׁעִים מֶ֣לֶךְ חָכָ֑ם וַיָּ֖שֶׁב עֲלֵיהֶ֣ם אוֹפָֽן׃
The human spirit[^19] is the lamp of the LORD, searching all the inner parts of the body.
נֵ֣ר יְ֭הוָה נִשְׁמַ֣ת אָדָ֑ם חֹ֝פֵ֗שׂ כָּל־חַדְרֵי־בָֽטֶן׃
Faithful love and truth[^20] guard a king; by faithful love his throne is upheld.
חֶ֣סֶד וֶ֭אֱמֶת יִצְּרוּ־מֶ֑לֶךְ וְסָעַ֖ד בַּחֶ֣סֶד כִּסְאֽוֹ׃
The glory of young men is their strength, and the splendor of the old is their gray hair.
תִּפְאֶ֣רֶת בַּחוּרִ֣ים כֹּחָ֑ם וַהֲדַ֖ר זְקֵנִ֣ים שֵׂיבָֽה׃
Blows that wound scour away evil, and beatings, the inner parts of the body.[^21]
חַבֻּר֣וֹת פֶּ֭צַע *תמריק **תַּמְר֣וּק בְּרָ֑ע וּ֝מַכּ֗וֹת חַדְרֵי־בָֽטֶן׃

n.1: Hebrew *lets*, the word used for the person who scorns wisdom (see 1:22).
n.2: Or "fermented drink"; brewed from grain.
n.3: Hebrew *ewil*, the morally perverse, stubborn fool (see 1:7).
n.4: Hebrew *atsel*, traditionally "sluggard" (see 6:6).
n.5: Hebrew *tevunah* (see 2:2).
n.6: Hebrew *chesed*, "faithful love".
n.7: Hebrew *tsaddiq*: one who does what is right (see 2:20).
n.8: Hebrew *ashrei*: happy, fortunate; traditionally "blessed".
n.9: Literally "a stone and a stone, an ephah and an ephah", one for buying and one for selling. Hebrew *ephah*, a measure for grain, used here for any measure of volume. Compare Deuteronomy 25:13–15.
n.10: *LORD*: God's personal name, Hebrew YHWH, written "the LORD" in capitals as in most English Bibles.
n.11: Or "Even a child may disguise himself by his actions".
n.12: Hebrew *peninim*, as in 3:15.
n.13: The Hebrew text is written "for foreigners" but read "for a foreign woman". Compare 27:13.
n.14: Hebrew *tachbulot*, as in 1:5.
n.15: The Hebrew text is written with a different word, perhaps "gained greedily", but read "gained in haste".
n.16: That is, to dedicate something to God without thinking.
n.17: Hebrew *resha'im*, plural of *rasha*: those who are guilty of wrong (see 2:22).
n.18: The wheel of a threshing cart, used to separate grain from straw (Isaiah 28:27–28).
n.19: Literally "The breath (*neshamah*) of a human being" (Genesis 2:7).
n.20: Hebrew *chesed ve-emet*: faithful love and reliability (see 3:3).
n.21: Literally "and blows, the chambers of the belly". The verb of the first line is understood again here.

v: The king's heart is like streams of water in the hand of the LORD;[^1] he turns it wherever he wishes.
פַּלְגֵי־מַ֣יִם לֶב־מֶ֭לֶךְ בְּיַד־יְהוָ֑ה עַֽל־כָּל־אֲשֶׁ֖ר יַחְפֹּ֣ץ יַטֶּֽנּוּ׃
All a person's ways seem right in his own eyes, but the LORD weighs hearts.
כָּֽל־דֶּרֶךְ־אִ֭ישׁ יָשָׁ֣ר בְּעֵינָ֑יו וְתֹכֵ֖ן לִבּ֣וֹת יְהוָֽה׃
Doing righteousness and justice is more acceptable to the LORD than sacrifice.
עֲ֭שֹׂה צְדָקָ֣ה וּמִשְׁפָּ֑ט נִבְחָ֖ר לַיהוָ֣ה מִזָּֽבַח׃
Haughty eyes and a proud heart, the lamp[^2] of the wicked,[^3] are sin.
רוּם־עֵ֭ינַיִם וּרְחַב־לֵ֑ב נִ֖ר רְשָׁעִ֣ים חַטָּֽאת׃
The plans of the diligent lead only to profit, but everyone who is hasty comes only to need.
מַחְשְׁב֣וֹת חָ֭רוּץ אַךְ־לְמוֹתָ֑ר וְכָל־אָ֝֗ץ אַךְ־לְמַחְסֽוֹר׃
Getting treasures by a lying tongue is a vapor[^4] blown away, for those who seek death.[^5]
פֹּ֣עַל א֭וֹצָרוֹת בִּלְשׁ֣וֹן שָׁ֑קֶר הֶ֥בֶל נִ֝דָּ֗ף מְבַקְשֵׁי־מָֽוֶת׃
The violence of the wicked will sweep them away, because they refuse to do what is just.
שֹׁד־רְשָׁעִ֥ים יְגוֹרֵ֑ם כִּ֥י מֵ֝אֲנ֗וּ לַעֲשׂ֥וֹת מִשְׁפָּֽט׃
The way of a guilty person[^6] is crooked, but the conduct of the pure is upright.
הֲפַכְפַּ֬ךְ דֶּ֣רֶךְ אִ֣ישׁ וָזָ֑ר וְ֝זַ֗ךְ יָשָׁ֥ר פָּעֳלֽוֹ׃
Better to live in a corner of the roof than in a house shared with a quarrelsome wife.
ט֗וֹב לָשֶׁ֥בֶת עַל־פִּנַּת־גָּ֑ג מֵאֵ֥שֶׁת מִ֝דְיָנִ֗ים וּבֵ֥ית חָֽבֶר׃
The soul of the wicked craves evil; his neighbor finds no mercy in his eyes.
נֶ֣פֶשׁ רָ֭שָׁע אִוְּתָה־רָ֑ע לֹא־יֻחַ֖ן בְּעֵינָ֣יו רֵעֵֽהוּ׃
When a mocker[^7] is punished, the simple[^8] becomes wise; when a wise person is instructed, he gains knowledge.
בַּעְנָשׁ־לֵ֭ץ יֶחְכַּם־פֶּ֑תִי וּבְהַשְׂכִּ֥יל לְ֝חָכָ֗ם יִקַּח־דָּֽעַת׃
The Righteous One[^9] observes the house of the wicked; he throws the wicked down to ruin.
מַשְׂכִּ֣יל צַ֭דִּיק לְבֵ֣ית רָשָׁ֑ע מְסַלֵּ֖ף רְשָׁעִ֣ים לָרָֽע׃
Whoever shuts his ears to the cry of the poor will himself call out and not be answered.
אֹטֵ֣ם אָ֭זְנוֹ מִזַּעֲקַת־דָּ֑ל גַּֽם־ה֥וּא יִ֝קְרָ֗א וְלֹ֣א יֵעָנֶֽה׃
A gift given in secret calms anger, and a bribe in the fold of the cloak calms fierce wrath.
מַתָּ֣ן בַּ֭סֵּתֶר יִכְפֶּה־אָ֑ף וְשֹׁ֥חַד בַּ֝חֵ֗ק חֵמָ֥ה עַזָּֽה׃
When justice is done, it is a joy to the righteous but terror to evildoers.
שִׂמְחָ֣ה לַ֭צַּדִּיק עֲשׂ֣וֹת מִשְׁפָּ֑ט וּ֝מְחִתָּ֗ה לְפֹ֣עֲלֵי אָֽוֶן׃
Whoever wanders from the way of good sense will rest in the assembly of the dead.[^10]
אָדָ֗ם תּ֖[d]וֹעֶה מִדֶּ֣רֶךְ הַשְׂכֵּ֑ל בִּקְהַ֖ל רְפָאִ֣ים יָנֽוּחַ׃
Whoever loves pleasure will be poor; whoever loves wine and oil will not grow rich.
אִ֣ישׁ מַ֭חְסוֹר אֹהֵ֣ב שִׂמְחָ֑ה אֹהֵ֥ב יַֽיִן־וָ֝שֶׁ֗מֶן לֹ֣א יַעֲשִֽׁיר׃
The wicked is a ransom for the righteous, and the treacherous takes the place of the upright.
כֹּ֣פֶר לַצַּדִּ֣יק רָשָׁ֑ע וְתַ֖חַת יְשָׁרִ֣ים בּוֹגֵֽד׃
Better to live in a desert land than with a quarrelsome and angry wife.
ט֗וֹב שֶׁ֥בֶת בְּאֶֽרֶץ־מִדְבָּ֑ר מֵאֵ֖שֶׁת *מדונים **מִדְיָנִ֣ים וָכָֽעַס׃
Precious treasure and oil are in the dwelling of the wise, but a foolish person[^11] swallows it up.
אוֹצָ֤ר ׀ נֶחְמָ֣ד וָ֭שֶׁמֶן בִּנְוֵ֣ה חָכָ֑ם וּכְסִ֖יל אָדָ֣ם יְבַלְּעֶֽנּוּ׃
Whoever pursues righteousness and faithful love will find life, righteousness[^12] and honor.
רֹ֭דֵף צְדָקָ֣ה וָחָ֑סֶד יִמְצָ֥א חַ֝יִּ֗ים צְדָקָ֥ה וְכָבֽוֹד׃
A wise person climbs the city of the mighty and brings down the stronghold they trusted in.
עִ֣יר גִּ֭בֹּרִים עָלָ֣ה חָכָ֑ם וַ֝יֹּ֗רֶד עֹ֣ז מִבְטֶחָֽה׃
Whoever guards his mouth and his tongue guards his life from troubles.
שֹׁמֵ֣ר פִּ֭יו וּלְשׁוֹנ֑וֹ שֹׁמֵ֖ר מִצָּר֣וֹת נַפְשֽׁוֹ׃
The proud and arrogant person, "Mocker" is his name; he acts with insolent fury.
זֵ֣ד יָ֭הִיר לֵ֣ץ שְׁמ֑וֹ ע֝וֹשֶׂ֗ה בְּעֶבְרַ֥ת זָדֽוֹן׃
The craving of the lazy person[^13] kills him, for his hands refuse to work.
תַּאֲוַ֣ת עָצֵ֣ל תְּמִיתֶ֑נּוּ כִּֽי־מֵאֲנ֖וּ יָדָ֣יו לַעֲשֽׂוֹת׃
All day long he craves and craves,[^14] but the righteous gives and does not hold back.
כָּל־הַ֭יּוֹם הִתְאַוָּ֣ה תַאֲוָ֑ה וְצַדִּ֥יק יִ֝תֵּ֗ן וְלֹ֣א יַחְשֹֽׂךְ׃
The sacrifice of the wicked is detestable; how much more when he brings it with evil intent!
זֶ֣בַח רְ֭שָׁעִים תּוֹעֵבָ֑ה אַ֝֗ף כִּֽי־בְזִמָּ֥ה יְבִיאֶֽנּוּ׃
A false witness will perish, but one who listens will speak forever.[^15]
עֵד־כְּזָבִ֥ים יֹאבֵ֑ד וְאִ֥ישׁ שׁ֝וֹמֵ֗עַ לָנֶ֥צַח יְדַבֵּֽר׃
A wicked man puts on a bold face, but the upright gives thought to his way.[^16]
הֵעֵ֬ז אִ֣ישׁ רָשָׁ֣ע בְּפָנָ֑יו וְ֝יָשָׁ֗ר ה֤וּא ׀ *יכין **יָבִ֬ין *דרכיו **דַּרְכּֽוֹ׃
There is no wisdom, no insight,[^17] no counsel that can stand against the LORD.
אֵ֣ין חָ֭כְמָה וְאֵ֣ין תְּבוּנָ֑ה וְאֵ֥ין עֵ֝צָ֗ה לְנֶ֣גֶד יְהוָֽה׃ פ
The horse is made ready for the day of battle, but victory belongs to the LORD.
ס֗וּס מ֭וּכָן לְי֣וֹם מִלְחָמָ֑ה וְ֝לַֽיהוָ֗ה הַתְּשׁוּעָֽה׃

n.1: *LORD*: God's personal name, Hebrew YHWH, written "the LORD" in capitals as in most English Bibles.
n.2: The Hebrew vowel points read *nir*, "newly plowed ground" (as in 13:23): "the plowing of the wicked". The same consonants can be read *ner*, "lamp" (13:9; 20:27).
n.3: Hebrew *resha'im*, plural of *rasha*: those who are guilty of wrong (see 2:22).
n.4: Hebrew *hevel*, "breath, vapor", the word used throughout Ecclesiastes.
n.5: The Septuagint and the Vulgate read "snares of death".
n.6: Hebrew *vazar*, a word found only here, probably "guilty". Or "The way of a man is crooked and strange".
n.7: Hebrew *lets*: one who scorns wisdom and laughs at correction (see 1:22). Also in verse 24.
n.8: Hebrew *peti*: a naive, inexperienced person, easily led (see 1:4).
n.9: Probably God (compare Job 34:17). Or "A righteous person observes the house of the wicked; the wicked are thrown down to ruin". Hebrew *tsaddiq* (see 2:20).
n.10: Hebrew *rephaim*, the spirits of the dead (see 2:18).
n.11: Literally "a fool (*kesil*) of a man" (see 1:22).
n.12: Or "prosperity", as in 8:18.
n.13: Hebrew *atsel*, traditionally "sluggard" (see 6:6).
n.14: Literally "he craves a craving", probably the lazy person of verse 25.
n.15: Or "will speak with lasting effect". Hebrew *lanetsach*, "forever, to the end".
n.16: The Hebrew text is written "makes his ways firm" but read "gives thought to his way".
n.17: Hebrew *tevunah* (see 2:2).

v: A good name is to be chosen rather than great riches, and favor is better than silver and gold.
נִבְחָ֣ר שֵׁ֭ם מֵעֹ֣שֶׁר רָ֑ב מִכֶּ֥סֶף וּ֝מִזָּהָ֗ב חֵ֣ן טֽוֹב׃
The rich and the poor meet together; the LORD[^1] is the maker of them all.
עָשִׁ֣יר וָרָ֣שׁ נִפְגָּ֑שׁוּ עֹשֵׂ֖ה כֻלָּ֣ם יְהוָֽה׃
The prudent[^2] sees danger and hides himself, but the simple[^3] go on and pay for it.
עָר֤וּם ׀ רָאָ֣ה רָעָ֣ה *ויסתר **וְנִסְתָּ֑ר וּ֝פְתָיִ֗ים עָבְר֥וּ וְֽנֶעֱנָֽשׁוּ׃
The reward for humility and the fear of the LORD is riches, honor and life.[^4]
עֵ֣קֶב עֲ֭נָוָה יִרְאַ֣ת יְהוָ֑ה עֹ֖שֶׁר וְכָב֣וֹד וְחַיִּֽים׃
Thorns and snares are in the way of the crooked; whoever guards his life will keep far from them.
צִנִּ֣ים פַּ֭חִים בְּדֶ֣רֶךְ עִקֵּ֑שׁ שׁוֹמֵ֥ר נַ֝פְשׁ֗וֹ יִרְחַ֥ק מֵהֶֽם׃
Train a child in the way he should go;[^5] even when he is old he will not turn away from it.
חֲנֹ֣ךְ לַ֭נַּעַר עַל־פִּ֣י דַרְכּ֑וֹ גַּ֥ם כִּֽי־יַ֝זְקִ֗ין לֹֽא־יָס֥וּר מִמֶּֽנָּה׃
The rich rules over the poor, and the borrower is servant[^6] to the lender.
עָ֭שִׁיר בְּרָשִׁ֣ים יִמְשׁ֑וֹל וְעֶ֥בֶד לֹ֝וֶ֗ה לְאִ֣ישׁ מַלְוֽ͏ֶה׃
Whoever sows injustice will reap trouble, and the rod of his fury will come to an end.[^7]
זוֹרֵ֣עַ עַ֭וְלָה *יקצו[y]*ר־**יִקְצָר־אָ֑וֶן וְשֵׁ֖בֶט עֶבְרָת֣וֹ יִכְלֶֽה׃
Whoever has a generous eye will be blessed, for he gives some of his bread to the poor.
טֽוֹב־עַ֭יִן ה֣וּא יְבֹרָ֑ךְ כִּֽי־נָתַ֖ן מִלַּחְמ֣וֹ לַדָּֽל׃
Drive out the mocker,[^8] and strife goes out; quarreling and insults will stop.
גָּ֣רֵֽשׁ לֵ֭ץ וְיֵצֵ֣א מָד֑וֹן וְ֝יִשְׁבֹּ֗ת דִּ֣ין וְקָלֽוֹן׃
Whoever loves purity of heart[^9] and whose speech is gracious will have the king as his friend.
אֹהֵ֥ב *טהור־**טְהָר־לֵ֑ב חֵ֥ן שְׂ֝פָתָ֗יו רֵעֵ֥הוּ מֶֽלֶךְ׃
The eyes of the LORD watch over knowledge, but he overturns the words of the treacherous.
עֵינֵ֣י יְ֭הוָה נָ֣צְרוּ דָ֑עַת וַ֝יְסַלֵּ֗ף דִּבְרֵ֥י בֹגֵֽד׃
The lazy person[^10] says, "There is a lion outside! I will be killed in the streets!"
אָמַ֣ר עָ֭צֵל אֲרִ֣י בַח֑וּץ בְּת֥וֹךְ רְ֝חֹב֗וֹת אֵֽרָצֵֽחַ׃
The mouth of strange women[^11] is a deep pit; whoever is cursed by the LORD will fall into it.
שׁוּחָ֣ה עֲ֭מֻקָּה פִּ֣י זָר֑וֹת זְע֥וּם יְ֝הוָ֗ה *יפול־**יִפָּל־שָֽׁם׃
Folly[^12] is bound up in the heart of a child, but the rod of discipline[^13] will drive it far from him.
אִ֭וֶּלֶת קְשׁוּרָ֣ה בְלֶב־נָ֑עַר שֵׁ֥בֶט מ֝וּסָ֗ר יַרְחִיקֶ֥נָּה מִמֶּֽנּוּ׃
Whoever oppresses the poor to increase his own wealth, or gives to the rich, comes only to need.[^14]
עֹ֣שֵֽׁק דָּ֭ל לְהַרְבּ֣וֹת ל֑וֹ נֹתֵ֥ן לְ֝עָשִׁ֗יר אַךְ־לְמַחְסֽוֹר׃
Turn your ear and listen to the words of the wise,[^15] and set your heart on my knowledge,
הַ֥ט אָזְנְךָ֗ וּ֖[d]שְׁמַע דִּבְרֵ֣י חֲכָמִ֑ים וְ֝לִבְּךָ֗ תָּשִׁ֥ית לְדַעְתִּֽי׃
for it is pleasant if you keep them within you,[^16] if all of them are ready on your lips.
כִּֽי־נָ֭עִים כִּֽי־תִשְׁמְרֵ֣ם בְּבִטְנֶ֑ךָ יִכֹּ֥נוּ יַ֝חְדָּ֗ו עַל־שְׂפָתֶֽיךָ׃
So that your trust may be in the LORD, I have taught you today, even you.
לִהְי֣וֹת בַּ֭יהוָה מִבְטַחֶ֑ךָ הוֹדַעְתִּ֖יךָ הַיּ֣וֹם אַף־אָֽתָּה׃
Have I not written for you excellent sayings[^17] of advice and knowledge,
הֲלֹ֤א כָתַ֣בְתִּי לְ֭ךָ *שלשום **שָׁלִישִׁ֑ים בְּמ֖וֹעֵצֹ֣ת וָדָֽעַת׃
to teach you what is right and true, so that you may bring back a true report to those who sent you?
לְהוֹדִֽיעֲךָ֗ קֹ֭שְׁטְ אִמְרֵ֣י אֱמֶ֑ת לְהָשִׁ֥יב אֲמָרִ֥ים אֱ֝מֶ֗ת לְשֹׁלְחֶֽיךָ׃ פ
Do not rob the poor because he is poor, and do not crush the afflicted at the gate,[^18]
אַֽל־תִּגְזָל־דָּ֭ל כִּ֣י דַל־ה֑וּא וְאַל־תְּדַכֵּ֖א עָנִ֣י בַשָּֽׁעַר׃
for the LORD will plead their case and will take the life of those who rob them.
כִּֽי־יְ֭הוָה יָרִ֣יב רִיבָ֑ם וְקָבַ֖ע אֶת־קֹבְעֵיהֶ֣ם נָֽפֶשׁ׃
Do not make friends with a hot-tempered person, and do not go about with a man given to anger,
אַל־תִּ֭תְרַע אֶת־בַּ֣עַל אָ֑ף וְאֶת־אִ֥ישׁ חֵ֝מוֹת לֹ֣א תָבֽוֹא׃
or you will learn his ways[^19] and get yourself caught in a snare.
פֶּן־תֶּאֱלַ֥ף *ארחתו **אֹֽרְחֹתָ֑יו וְלָקַחְתָּ֖ מוֹקֵ֣שׁ לְנַפְשֶֽׁךָ׃
Do not be one of those who shake hands on a pledge, who put up security for debts.
אַל־תְּהִ֥י בְתֹֽקְעֵי־כָ֑ף בַּ֝עֹרְבִ֗ים מַשָּׁאֽוֹת׃
If you have nothing with which to pay, why should your bed be taken from under you?
אִם־אֵֽין־לְךָ֥ לְשַׁלֵּ֑ם לָ֥מָּה יִקַּ֥ח מִ֝שְׁכָּבְךָ֗ מִתַּחְתֶּֽיךָ׃
Do not move the ancient boundary stone that your ancestors set up.
אַל־תַּ֭סֵּג גְּב֣וּל עוֹלָ֑ם אֲשֶׁ֖ר עָשׂ֣וּ אֲבוֹתֶֽיךָ׃
Do you see a man skilled in his work? He will serve before kings; he will not serve before obscure people.
חָזִ֡יתָ אִ֤ישׁ ׀ מָ֘הִ֤יר בִּמְלַאכְתּ֗וֹ לִֽפְנֵֽי־מְלָכִ֥ים יִתְיַצָּ֑ב בַּל־יִ֝תְיַצֵּב לִפְנֵ֥י חֲשֻׁכִּֽים׃ פ

n.1: *LORD*: God's personal name, Hebrew YHWH, written "the LORD" in capitals as in most English Bibles.
n.2: Hebrew *arum*, "shrewd, prudent" (see 1:4). The verse is repeated in 27:12.
n.3: Hebrew *peta'im*, plural of *peti*: naive, inexperienced people, easily led (see 1:4).
n.4: Literally "The reward of humility, the fear of the LORD, riches and honor and life". Or "The reward of humility, which is the fear of the LORD, is riches …".
n.5: Literally "according to his way": the way he should go, or the way that suits him.
n.6: Or "slave".
n.7: The Septuagint adds a line, "God blesses a man who is cheerful and generous", echoed in 2 Corinthians 9:7.
n.8: Hebrew *lets*: one who scorns wisdom and laughs at correction (see 1:22).
n.9: The Hebrew text is written "the pure of heart" but read "purity of heart".
n.10: Hebrew *atsel*, traditionally "sluggard" (see 6:6).
n.11: Hebrew *zarot*, plural of *zarah*, "strange woman", a woman outside one's marriage (see 2:16).
n.12: Hebrew *iwwelet*, "folly", the word related to *ewil*, "fool" (see 1:7).
n.13: Hebrew *musar*: discipline, training and correction (see 1:2).
n.14: The Hebrew is compact. Or "Oppressing the poor may increase a person's wealth, but giving to the rich leads only to need".
n.15: A new collection begins here (22:17–24:22), "the words of the wise" (compare 24:23). Much of 22:17–23:11 closely resembles an Egyptian work, the Instruction of Amenemope, which is arranged in thirty chapters (compare verse 20).
n.16: Literally "in your belly".
n.17: The Hebrew text is written *shilshom*, "formerly", but read *shalishim*, a word that usually means "officers" and is traditionally taken here as "excellent things". Many scholars read *sheloshim*, "thirty (sayings)", with a small change to the Hebrew (compare the note on verse 17).
n.18: The town gate, where the court met.
n.19: The Hebrew text is written "his way" but read "his ways".

v: When you sit down to eat with a ruler, consider carefully what is before you,[^1]
כִּֽי־תֵ֭שֵׁב לִלְח֣וֹם אֶת־מוֹשֵׁ֑ל בִּ֥ין תָּ֝בִ֗ין אֶת־אֲשֶׁ֥ר לְפָנֶֽיךָ׃
and put a knife to your throat if you have a big appetite.[^2]
וְשַׂמְתָּ֣ שַׂכִּ֣ין בְּלֹעֶ֑ךָ אִם־בַּ֖עַל נֶ֣פֶשׁ אָֽתָּה׃
Do not crave his delicacies, for they are deceptive food.
אַל־תִּ֭תְאָו לְמַטְעַמּוֹתָ֑יו וְ֝ה֗וּא לֶ֣חֶם כְּזָבִֽים׃
Do not wear yourself out to get rich; stop relying on your own understanding.[^3]
אַל־תִּיגַ֥ע לְֽהַעֲשִׁ֑יר מִֽבִּינָתְךָ֥ חֲדָֽל׃
When your eyes fly to it, it is gone;[^4] for it will surely make itself wings and fly off to the sky like an eagle.
*התעוף **הֲתָ֤עִיף עֵינֶ֥יךָ בּ֗וֹ וְֽאֵ֫ינֶ֥נּוּ כִּ֤י עָשֹׂ֣ה יַעֲשֶׂה־לּ֣וֹ כְנָפַ֑יִם כְּ֝נֶ֗שֶׁר *ועיף **יָע֥וּף הַשָּׁמָֽיִם׃ פ
Do not eat the bread of a stingy person,[^5] and do not crave his delicacies,
אַל־תִּלְחַ֗ם אֶת־לֶ֭חֶם רַ֣ע עָ֑יִן וְאַל־*תתאו **תִּ֝תְאָ֗יו לְמַטְעַמֹּתָֽיו׃
for he is like one who keeps count in his mind.[^6] "Eat and drink!" he says to you, but his heart is not with you.
כִּ֤י ׀ כְּמּֽ[m]וֹ שָׁעַ֥ר בְּנַפְשׁ֗וֹ כֶּ֫ן־ה֥וּא אֱכֹ֣ל וּ֭שְׁתֵה יֹ֣אמַר לָ֑ךְ וְ֝לִבּ֗וֹ בַּל־עִמָּֽךְ׃
You will vomit up the morsel you have eaten and waste your pleasant words.
פִּֽתְּךָ־אָכַ֥לְתָּ תְקִיאֶ֑נָּה וְ֝שִׁחַ֗תָּ דְּבָרֶ֥יךָ הַנְּעִימִֽים׃
Do not speak in the hearing of a fool,[^7] for he will despise the good sense of your words.
בְּאָזְנֵ֣י כְ֭סִיל אַל־תְּדַבֵּ֑ר כִּֽי־יָ֝ב֗וּז לְשֵׂ֣כֶל מִלֶּֽיךָ׃
Do not move an ancient boundary stone[^8] or encroach on the fields of the fatherless,
אַל־תַּ֭סֵּג גְּב֣וּל עוֹלָ֑ם וּבִשְׂדֵ֥י יְ֝תוֹמִ֗ים אַל־תָּבֹֽא׃
for their redeemer[^9] is strong; he will plead their case against you.
כִּֽי־גֹאֲלָ֥ם חָזָ֑ק הֽוּא־יָרִ֖יב אֶת־רִיבָ֣ם אִתָּֽךְ׃
Apply your heart to discipline[^10] and your ears to words of knowledge.
הָבִ֣יאָה לַמּוּסָ֣ר לִבֶּ֑ךָ וְ֝אָזְנֶ֗ךָ לְאִמְרֵי־דָֽעַת׃
Do not withhold discipline from a child; if you strike him with a rod, he will not die.
אַל־תִּמְנַ֣ע מִנַּ֣עַר מוּסָ֑ר כִּֽי־תַכֶּ֥נּוּ בַ֝שֵּׁ֗בֶט לֹ֣א יָמֽוּת׃
Strike him with the rod, and you will rescue his life from Sheol.[^11]
אַ֭תָּה בַּשֵּׁ֣בֶט תַּכֶּ֑נּוּ וְ֝נַפְשׁ֗וֹ מִשְּׁא֥וֹל תַּצִּֽיל׃
My son, if your heart is wise, my heart too will be glad,
בְּ֭נִי אִם־חָכַ֣ם לִבֶּ֑ךָ יִשְׂמַ֖ח לִבִּ֣י גַם־אָֽנִי׃
and my inmost being[^12] will rejoice when your lips speak what is right.
וְתַעְלֹ֥זְנָה כִלְיוֹתָ֑י בְּדַבֵּ֥ר שְׂ֝פָתֶ֗יךָ מֵישָׁרִֽים׃
Do not let your heart envy sinners, but continue[^13] in the fear of the LORD[^14] all day long.
אַל־יְקַנֵּ֣א לִ֭בְּךָ בַּֽחַטָּאִ֑ים כִּ֥י אִם־בְּיִרְאַת־יְ֝הוָ֗ה כָּל־הַיּֽוֹם׃
For surely there is a future, and your hope will not be cut off.
כִּ֭י אִם־יֵ֣שׁ אַחֲרִ֑ית וְ֝תִקְוָתְךָ֗ לֹ֣א תִכָּרֵֽת׃
Listen, my son, and be wise, and direct your heart in the way.
שְׁמַע־אַתָּ֣ה בְנִ֣י וַחֲכָ֑ם וְאַשֵּׁ֖ר בַּדֶּ֣רֶךְ לִבֶּֽךָ׃
Do not be among those who drink too much wine or those who gorge themselves on meat,
אַל־תְּהִ֥י בְסֹֽבְאֵי־יָ֑יִן בְּזֹלֲלֵ֖י בָשָׂ֣ר לָֽמוֹ׃
for the drunkard and the glutton will become poor, and drowsiness clothes them in rags.
כִּי־סֹבֵ֣א וְ֭זוֹלֵל יִוָּרֵ֑שׁ וּ֝קְרָעִ֗ים תַּלְבִּ֥ישׁ נוּמָֽה׃
Listen to your father, who gave you life, and do not despise your mother when she is old.
שְׁמַ֣ע לְ֭אָבִיךָ זֶ֣ה יְלָדֶ֑ךָ וְאַל־תָּ֝ב֗וּז כִּֽי־זָקְנָ֥ה אִמֶּֽךָ׃
Buy truth and do not sell it, wisdom, discipline and understanding.
אֱמֶ֣ת קְ֭נֵה וְאַל־תִּמְכֹּ֑ר חָכְמָ֖ה וּמוּסָ֣ר וּבִינָֽה׃
The father of a righteous person[^15] will greatly rejoice; whoever fathers a wise son will be glad in him.
*גול **גִּ֣יל *יגול **יָ֭גִיל אֲבִ֣י צַדִּ֑יק *יולד **וְיוֹלֵ֥ד חָ֝כָ֗ם *וישמח־**יִשְׂמַח־בּֽוֹ׃
Let your father and mother be glad; let her who bore you rejoice.
יִֽשְׂמַח־אָבִ֥יךָ וְאִמֶּ֑ךָ וְ֝תָגֵ֗ל יֽוֹלַדְתֶּֽךָ׃
My son, give me your heart, and let your eyes keep to my ways.[^16]
תְּנָֽה־בְנִ֣י לִבְּךָ֣ לִ֑י וְ֝עֵינֶ֗יךָ דְּרָכַ֥י *תרצנה **תִּצֽרְ[q]**ֹנָה׃
For a prostitute is a deep pit, and a foreign woman[^17] is a narrow well.
כִּֽי־שׁוּחָ֣ה עֲמֻקָּ֣ה זוֹנָ֑ה וּבְאֵ֥ר צָ֝רָ֗ה נָכְרִיָּֽה׃
She lies in wait like a robber and increases the number of the treacherous among men.
אַף־הִ֭יא כְּחֶ֣תֶף תֶּֽאֱרֹ֑ב וּ֝בוֹגְדִ֗ים בְּאָדָ֥ם תּוֹסִֽף׃
Who has woe? Who has sorrow? Who has quarrels? Who has complaints? Who has wounds for no reason? Who has bloodshot eyes?
לְמִ֨י א֥וֹי לְמִ֪י אֲב֡וֹי לְמִ֤י *מדונים **מִדְיָנִ֨ים ׀ לְמִ֥י שִׂ֗יחַ לְ֭מִי פְּצָעִ֣ים חִנָּ֑ם לְ֝מִ֗י חַכְלִל֥וּת עֵינָֽיִם׃
Those who linger over wine, who go to taste mixed wine.
לַֽמְאַחֲרִ֥ים עַל־הַיָּ֑יִן לַ֝בָּאִ֗ים לַחְקֹ֥ר מִמְסָֽךְ׃
Do not look at wine when it is red, when it sparkles in the cup,[^18] when it goes down smoothly.
אַל־תֵּ֥רֶא יַּיִן֮ כִּ֢י יִתְאַ֫דָּ֥ם כִּֽי־יִתֵּ֣ן *בכיס **בַּכּ֣וֹס עֵינ֑וֹ יִ֝תְהַלֵּ֗ךְ בְּמֵישָׁרִֽים׃
In the end it bites like a snake and stings like a viper.
אַ֭חֲרִיתוֹ כְּנָחָ֣שׁ יִשָּׁ֑ךְ וּֽכְצִפְעֹנִ֥י יַפְרִֽשׁ׃
Your eyes will see strange things,[^19] and your heart will speak perverse things.
עֵ֭ינֶיךָ יִרְא֣וּ זָר֑וֹת וְ֝לִבְּךָ֗ יְדַבֵּ֥ר תַּהְפֻּכֽוֹת׃
You will be like one who lies down in the middle of the sea, like one who lies on top of a mast.[^20]
וְ֭הָיִיתָ כְּשֹׁכֵ֣ב בְּלֶב־יָ֑ם וּ֝כְשֹׁכֵ֗ב בְּרֹ֣אשׁ חִבֵּֽל׃
"They hit me," you will say,[^21] "but I was not hurt; they beat me, but I did not feel it. When will I wake up? I will look for another drink."[^22]
הִכּ֥וּנִי בַל־חָלִיתִי֮ הֲלָמ֗וּנִי בַּל־יָ֫דָ֥עְתִּי מָתַ֥י אָקִ֑יץ א֝וֹסִ֗יף אֲבַקְשֶׁ֥נּוּ עֽוֹד׃

n.1: Or "who is before you".
n.2: Literally "if you are a master of appetite (*nephesh*)".
n.3: Literally "from your understanding (*binah*), stop". Or "have the sense to stop".
n.4: Literally "Will you let your eyes fly to it, and it is not?"
n.5: Literally "one who is evil of eye".
n.6: The Hebrew of this line is uncertain. Literally "for as he has calculated in his soul, so is he". With different vowels, the same consonants can be read "like a hair in his throat".
n.7: Hebrew *kesil* (see 1:22).
n.8: Compare 22:28.
n.9: Hebrew *go'el*, a relative whose duty was to defend a family member and buy back what he had lost (Leviticus 25:25; Ruth 4:4–6). Here probably God (compare 22:23).
n.10: Hebrew *musar*: discipline, training and correction (see 1:2). Also in verses 13 and 23.
n.11: Hebrew *Sheol*, the realm of the dead.
n.12: Literally "my kidneys", thought of as the seat of the emotions.
n.13: Literally "but in the fear of the LORD all day".
n.14: *LORD*: God's personal name, Hebrew YHWH, written "the LORD" in capitals as in most English Bibles.
n.15: Hebrew *tsaddiq*: one who does what is right (see 2:20).
n.16: The Hebrew text is written "delight in my ways" but read "keep to my ways".
n.17: Hebrew *nokhriyyah*, "foreign woman" (see 2:16).
n.18: The Hebrew text is written "in the purse" but read "in the cup". Literally "when it gives its eye in the cup".
n.20: Hebrew *chibbel*, a word found only here, probably "mast" or "rigging".
n.21: The words *you will say* are not in the Hebrew. The verse gives the drunkard's own words.

v: Do not envy evil people, and do not desire to be with them,
אַל־תְּ֭קַנֵּא בְּאַנְשֵׁ֣י רָעָ֑ה וְאַל־*תתאו **תִּ֝תְאָ֗יו לִהְי֥וֹת אִתָּֽם׃
for their hearts plot violence, and their lips talk of trouble.
כִּי־שֹׁ֭ד יֶהְגֶּ֣ה לִבָּ֑ם וְ֝עָמָ֗ל שִׂפְתֵיהֶ֥ם תְּדַבֵּֽרְנָה׃
By wisdom a house is built, and by insight[^1] it is established;
בְּ֭חָכְמָה יִבָּ֣נֶה בָּ֑יִת וּ֝בִתְבוּנָ֗ה יִתְכּוֹנָֽן׃
by knowledge its rooms are filled with all kinds of precious and pleasant wealth.
וּ֭בְדַעַת חֲדָרִ֣ים יִמָּלְא֑וּ כָּל־ה֖וֹן יָקָ֣ר וְנָעִֽים׃
A wise man is strong,[^2] and a person of knowledge increases his strength,
גֶּֽבֶר־חָכָ֥ם בַּע֑וֹז וְאִֽישׁ־דַּ֝֗עַת מְאַמֶּץ־כֹּֽחַ׃
for by guidance[^3] you wage your war, and with many advisers there is victory.
כִּ֣י בְ֭תַחְבֻּלוֹת תַּעֲשֶׂה־לְּךָ֣ מִלְחָמָ֑ה וּ֝תְשׁוּעָ֗ה בְּרֹ֣ב יוֹעֵֽץ׃
Wisdom[^4] is too high for a fool;[^5] in the gate he does not open his mouth.
רָאמ֣וֹת לֶֽאֱוִ֣יל חָכְמ֑וֹת בַּ֝שַּׁ֗עַר לֹ֣א יִפְתַּח־פִּֽיהוּ׃
Whoever plans to do evil will be called a schemer.[^6]
מְחַשֵּׁ֥ב לְהָרֵ֑עַ ל֝֗וֹ בַּֽעַל־מְזִמּ֥וֹת יִקְרָֽאוּ׃
The scheming of folly[^7] is sin, and a mocker[^8] is detestable to people.
זִמַּ֣ת אִוֶּ֣לֶת חַטָּ֑את וְתוֹעֲבַ֖ת לְאָדָ֣ם לֵֽץ׃
If you lose heart in the day of trouble, your strength is small.[^9]
הִ֭תְרַפִּיתָ בְּי֥וֹם צָרָ֗ה צַ֣ר כֹּחֶֽכָה׃
Rescue those who are being taken away to death; hold back those who are staggering to the slaughter.
הַ֭צֵּל לְקֻחִ֣ים לַמָּ֑וֶת וּמָטִ֥ים לַ֝הֶ֗רֶג אִם־תַּחְשֽׂוֹךְ׃
If you say, "But we did not know this," does not the one who weighs hearts understand? Does not the one who guards your life know it? He will repay each person according to what he has done.[^10]
כִּֽי־תֹאמַ֗ר הֵן֮ לֹא־יָדַ֢עְנ֫וּ זֶ֥ה הֲ‍ֽלֹא־תֹ֘כֵ֤ן לִבּ֨וֹת ׀ הֽוּא־יָבִ֗ין וְנֹצֵ֣ר נַ֭פְשְׁךָ ה֣וּא יֵדָ֑ע וְהֵשִׁ֖יב לְאָדָ֣ם כְּפָעֳלֽוֹ׃
Eat honey, my son, for it is good, and the honeycomb is sweet to your taste.
אֱכָל־בְּנִ֣י דְבַ֣שׁ כִּי־ט֑וֹב וְנֹ֥פֶת מָ֝ת֗וֹק עַל־חִכֶּֽךָ׃
Know that wisdom is like that for your soul; if you find it, there will be a future, and your hope will not be cut off.
כֵּ֤ן ׀ דְּעֶ֥ה חָכְמָ֗ה לְנַ֫פְשֶׁ֥ךָ אִם־מָ֭צָאתָ וְיֵ֣שׁ אַחֲרִ֑ית וְ֝תִקְוָתְךָ֗ לֹ֣א תִכָּרֵֽת׃ פ
Do not lie in wait like a wicked man[^11] against the home of the righteous;[^12] do not destroy his resting place.
אַל־תֶּאֱרֹ֣ב רָ֭שָׁע לִנְוֵ֣ה צַדִּ֑יק אַֽל־תְּשַׁדֵּ֥ד רִבְצוֹ׃
For the righteous falls seven times and rises again, but the wicked stumble in times of disaster.
כִּ֤י שֶׁ֨בַע ׀ יִפּ֣וֹל צַדִּ֣יק וָקָ֑ם וּ֝רְשָׁעִ֗ים יִכָּשְׁל֥וּ בְרָעָֽה׃
Do not rejoice when your enemy[^13] falls, and do not let your heart be glad when he stumbles,
בִּנְפֹ֣ל *אויבי[y]*ך **אֽ֭וֹיִבְךָ אַל־תִּשְׂמָ֑ח וּ֝בִכָּשְׁל֗וֹ אַל־יָגֵ֥ל לִבֶּֽךָ׃
or the LORD[^14] will see it and be displeased, and turn his anger away from him.
פֶּן־יִרְאֶ֣ה יְ֭הוָה וְרַ֣ע בְּעֵינָ֑יו וְהֵשִׁ֖יב מֵעָלָ֣יו אַפּֽוֹ׃
Do not fret because of evildoers or envy the wicked,
אַל־תִּתְחַ֥ר בַּמְּרֵעִ֑ים אַל־תְּ֝קַנֵּ֗א בָּרְשָׁעִֽים׃
for the evil person has no future; the lamp of the wicked will be snuffed out.
כִּ֤י ׀ לֹֽא־תִהְיֶ֣ה אַחֲרִ֣ית לָרָ֑ע נֵ֖ר רְשָׁעִ֣ים יִדְעָֽךְ׃
My son, fear the LORD and the king; do not associate with those who are given to change,[^15]
יְרָֽא־אֶת־יְהוָ֣ה בְּנִ֣י וָמֶ֑לֶךְ עִם־שׁ֝וֹנִ֗ים אַל־תִּתְעָרָֽב׃
for disaster from them will rise suddenly, and who knows the ruin the two of them can bring?[^16]
כִּֽי־פִ֭תְאֹם יָק֣וּם אֵידָ֑ם וּפִ֥יד שְׁ֝נֵיהֶ֗ם מִ֣י יוֹדֵֽעַ׃ ס
These also are sayings of the wise.[^17] Showing partiality[^18] in judgment is not good.
גַּם־אֵ֥לֶּה לַֽחֲכָמִ֑ים הַֽכֵּר־פָּנִ֖ים בְּמִשְׁפָּ֣ט בַּל־טֽוֹב׃
Whoever says to the wicked, "You are righteous," peoples will curse him, nations will denounce him.
אֹ֤מֵ֨ר ׀ לְרָשָׁע֮ צַדִּ֢יק אָ֥תָּה יִקְּבֻ֥הוּ עַמִּ֑ים יִזְעָמ֥וּהוּ לְאֻמִּֽים׃
But those who rebuke the wicked will find delight, and a good blessing will come upon them.
וְלַמּוֹכִיחִ֥ים יִנְעָ֑ם וַֽ֝עֲלֵיהֶ֗ם תָּב֥וֹא בִרְכַּת־טֹֽוּב׃
Whoever gives an honest answer kisses the lips.[^19]
שְׂפָתַ֥יִם יִשָּׁ֑ק מֵ֝שִׁ֗יב דְּבָרִ֥ים נְכֹחִֽים׃
Put your outdoor work in order and get your fields ready; after that, build your house.[^20]
הָ֘כֵ֤ן בַּח֨וּץ ׀ מְלַאכְתֶּ֗ךָ וְעַתְּדָ֣הּ בַּשָּׂדֶ֣ה לָ֑ךְ אַ֝חַ֗ר וּבָנִ֥יתָ בֵיתֶֽךָ׃ פ
Do not be a witness against your neighbor without cause; would you deceive with your lips?
אַל־תְּהִ֣י עֵד־חִנָּ֣ם בְּרֵעֶ֑ךָ וַ֝הֲפִתִּ֗יתָ בִּשְׂפָתֶֽיךָ׃
Do not say, "I will do to him as he has done to me; I will pay the man back for what he has done."
אַל־תֹּאמַ֗ר כַּאֲשֶׁ֣ר עָֽשָׂה־לִ֭י כֵּ֤ן אֶֽעֱשֶׂה־לּ֑וֹ אָשִׁ֖יב לָאִ֣ישׁ כְּפָעֳלֽוֹ׃
I passed by the field of a lazy man,[^21] by the vineyard of a man who lacked sense,[^22]
עַל־שְׂדֵ֣ה אִישׁ־עָצֵ֣ל עָבַ֑רְתִּי וְעַל־כֶּ֝֗רֶם אָדָ֥ם חֲסַר־לֵֽב׃
and look, it was all overgrown with thistles; its surface was covered with weeds, and its stone wall was broken down.
וְהִנֵּ֨ה עָ֘לָ֤ה כֻלּ֨וֹ ׀ קִמְּשֹׂנִ֗ים כָּסּ֣וּ פָנָ֣יו חֲרֻלִּ֑ים וְגֶ֖דֶר אֲבָנָ֣יו נֶהֱרָֽסָה׃
I looked and took it to heart; I saw and received discipline:[^23]
וָֽאֶחֱזֶ֣ה אָ֭נֹכִֽי אָשִׁ֣ית לִבִּ֑י רָ֝אִ֗יתִי לָקַ֥חְתִּי מוּסָּֽר׃
a little sleep, a little slumber, a little folding of the hands to rest,
מְעַ֣ט שֵׁ֭נוֹת מְעַ֣ט תְּנוּמ֑וֹת מְעַ֓ט ׀ חִבֻּ֖ק יָדַ֣יִם לִשְׁכָּֽב׃
and poverty will come on you like a prowler, and need like an armed man.[^24]
וּבָֽא־מִתְהַלֵּ֥ךְ רֵישֶׁ֑ךָ וּ֝מַחְסֹרֶ֗יךָ כְּאִ֣ישׁ מָגֵֽן׃ פ

n.1: Hebrew *tevunah* (see 2:2).
n.2: Literally "is in strength". The Septuagint reads "A wise man is better than a strong one".
n.3: Hebrew *tachbulot*, as in 1:5.
n.4: Hebrew *chokhmot*, as in 1:20.
n.5: Hebrew *ewil*, the morally perverse, stubborn fool (see 1:7).
n.6: Literally "a master of schemes". Hebrew *mezimmot*, as in 12:2.
n.7: Hebrew *iwwelet*, "folly", the word related to *ewil*, "fool" (see 1:7).
n.8: Hebrew *lets*: one who scorns wisdom and laughs at correction (see 1:22).
n.9: In Hebrew there is a play on *tsarah*, "trouble", and *tsar*, "small, narrow".
n.10: Compare Psalm 62:13 (62:12 in most English Bibles); Romans 2:6.
n.11: Or "Do not lie in wait, you wicked man". Hebrew *rasha* (see 2:22).
n.12: Hebrew *tsaddiq*: one who does what is right (see 2:20).
n.13: The Hebrew text is written "your enemies" but read "your enemy".
n.14: *LORD*: God's personal name, Hebrew YHWH, written "the LORD" in capitals as in most English Bibles.
n.15: Hebrew *shonim*, "those who change", perhaps rebels. The Septuagint reads "and do not disobey either of them".
n.16: *The two of them* are probably the LORD and the king (verse 21).
n.17: A short collection follows (verses 23–34). From here to the end of the book the Septuagint arranges the material differently. After 24:22 it has 30:1–14, then 24:23–34, then 30:15–33 and 31:1–9, then chapters 25–29, and last 31:10–31.
n.18: Literally "Recognizing faces".
n.19: A kiss on the lips may have been a sign of friendship and loyalty.
n.22: Literally "lacking heart". In Hebrew thought the heart is the seat of understanding.

v: These also are proverbs of Solomon, which the men of Hezekiah king of Judah copied.[^1]
גַּם־אֵ֭לֶּה מִשְׁלֵ֣י שְׁלֹמֹ֑ה אֲשֶׁ֥ר הֶ֝עְתִּ֗יקוּ אַנְשֵׁ֤י ׀ חִזְקִיָּ֬ה מֶֽלֶךְ־יְהוּדָֽה׃
It is the glory of God to conceal a matter, and the glory of kings to search out a matter.
כְּבֹ֣ד אֱ֭לֹהִים הַסְתֵּ֣ר דָּבָ֑ר וּכְבֹ֥ד מְ֝לָכִ֗ים חֲקֹ֣ר דָּבָֽר׃
As the heavens are high and the earth is deep, so the heart of kings is unsearchable.
שָׁמַ֣יִם לָ֭רוּם וָאָ֣רֶץ לָעֹ֑מֶק וְלֵ֥ב מְ֝לָכִ֗ים אֵ֣ין חֵֽקֶר׃
Remove the dross from silver, and a vessel comes out for the silversmith.
הָג֣וֹ סִיגִ֣ים מִכָּ֑סֶף וַיֵּצֵ֖א לַצֹּרֵ֣ף כֶּֽלִי׃
Remove the wicked[^2] from the king's presence, and his throne will be established in righteousness.
הָג֣וֹ רָ֭שָׁע לִפְנֵי־מֶ֑לֶךְ וְיִכּ֖וֹן בַּצֶּ֣דֶק כִּסְאֽוֹ׃
Do not put yourself forward before the king, and do not stand in the place of the great,
אַל־תִּתְהַדַּ֥ר לִפְנֵי־מֶ֑לֶךְ וּבִמְק֥וֹם גְּ֝דֹלִ֗ים אַֽל־תַּעֲמֹֽד׃
for it is better to be told, "Come up here," than to be put lower in the presence of a noble whom your eyes have seen.[^3]
כִּ֤י ט֥וֹב אֲמָר־לְךָ֗ עֲ‍ֽלֵ֫ה הֵ֥נָּה מֵֽ֭הַשְׁפִּ֣ילְךָ לִפְנֵ֣י נָדִ֑יב אֲשֶׁ֖ר רָא֣וּ עֵינֶֽיךָ׃
Do not go out hastily to court, for what will you do in the end, when your neighbor puts you to shame?
אַל־תֵּצֵ֥א לָרִ֗ב מַ֫הֵ֥ר פֶּ֣ן מַה־תַּ֭עֲשֶׂה בְּאַחֲרִיתָ֑הּ בְּהַכְלִ֖ים אֹתְךָ֣ רֵעֶֽךָ׃
Argue your case with your neighbor, but do not reveal another's secret,
רִֽ֭יבְךָ רִ֣יב אֶת־רֵעֶ֑ךָ וְס֖וֹד אַחֵ֣ר אַל־תְּגָֽל׃
or the one who hears it will disgrace you,[^4] and your bad name will never go away.
פֶּֽן־יְחַסֶּדְךָ֥ שֹׁמֵ֑עַ וְ֝דִבָּתְךָ֗ לֹ֣א תָשֽׁוּב׃
Like apples of gold in settings of silver is a word spoken at the right time.[^5]
תַּפּוּחֵ֣י זָ֭הָב בְּמַשְׂכִּיּ֣וֹת כָּ֑סֶף דָּ֝בָ֗ר דָּבֻ֥ר עַל־אָפְנָֽיו׃
Like a gold earring or an ornament of fine gold is a wise person who corrects a listening ear.
נֶ֣זֶם זָ֭הָב וַחֲלִי־כָ֑תֶם מוֹכִ֥יחַ חָ֝כָ֗ם עַל־אֹ֥זֶן שֹׁמָֽעַת׃
Like the coolness of snow at harvest time is a faithful messenger to those who send him; he refreshes the life of his masters.
כְּצִנַּת־שֶׁ֨לֶג ׀ בְּי֬וֹם קָצִ֗יר צִ֣יר נֶ֭אֱמָן לְשֹׁלְחָ֑יו וְנֶ֖פֶשׁ אֲדֹנָ֣יו יָשִֽׁיב׃ פ
Like clouds and wind without rain is a man who boasts of a gift he does not give.
נְשִׂיאִ֣ים וְ֭רוּחַ וְגֶ֣שֶׁם אָ֑יִן אִ֥ישׁ מִ֝תְהַלֵּ֗ל בְּמַתַּת־שָֽׁקֶר׃
With patience a ruler can be persuaded, and a gentle tongue can break a bone.
בְּאֹ֣רֶךְ אַ֭פַּיִם יְפֻתֶּ֣ה קָצִ֑ין וְלָשׁ֥וֹן רַ֝כָּ֗ה תִּשְׁבָּר־גָּֽרֶם׃
If you find honey, eat only what you need, or you will have too much and vomit it up.
דְּבַ֣שׁ מָ֭צָאתָ אֱכֹ֣ל דַּיֶּ֑ךָּ פֶּן־תִּ֝שְׂבָּעֶ֗נּוּ וַהֲקֵֽאתֽוֹ׃
Seldom set foot in your neighbor's house, or he will have too much of you and hate you.
הֹקַ֣ר רַ֭גְלְךָ מִבֵּ֣ית רֵעֶ֑ךָ פֶּן־יִ֝שְׂבָּעֲךָ֗ וּשְׂנֵאֶֽךָ׃
Like a club, a sword or a sharp arrow is a man who gives false testimony against his neighbor.
מֵפִ֣יץ וְ֭חֶרֶב וְחֵ֣ץ שָׁנ֑וּן אִ֥ישׁ עֹנֶ֥ה בְ֝רֵעֵ֗הוּ עֵ֣ד שָֽׁקֶר׃
Like a broken tooth or a lame foot is trust in a treacherous person in a time of trouble.
שֵׁ֣ן רֹ֭עָה וְרֶ֣גֶל מוּעָ֑דֶת מִבְטָ֥ח בּ֝וֹגֵ֗ד בְּי֣וֹם צָרֽ͏ָה׃
Like one who takes off a garment on a cold day, like vinegar on soda,[^6] is one who sings songs to a heavy heart.
מַ֥עֲדֶה בֶּ֨גֶד ׀ בְּי֣וֹם קָ֭רָה חֹ֣מֶץ עַל־נָ֑תֶר וְשָׁ֥ר בַּ֝שִּׁרִ֗ים עַ֣ל לֶב־רָֽע׃ פ
If your enemy[^7] is hungry, give him bread to eat; if he is thirsty, give him water to drink,
אִם־רָעֵ֣ב שֹׂ֭נַאֲךָ הַאֲכִלֵ֣הוּ לָ֑חֶם וְאִם־צָ֝מֵ֗א הַשְׁקֵ֥הוּ מָֽיִם׃
for you will heap burning coals on his head, and the LORD[^8] will reward you.[^9]
כִּ֤י גֶֽחָלִ֗ים אַ֭תָּה חֹתֶ֣ה עַל־רֹאשׁ֑וֹ וֽ͏ַ֝יהוָ֗ה יְשַׁלֶּם־לָֽךְ׃
The north wind brings forth rain, and a secret tongue, angry faces.
ר֣וּחַ צָ֭פוֹן תְּח֣וֹלֵֽל גָּ֑שֶׁם וּפָנִ֥ים נִ֝זְעָמִ֗ים לְשׁ֣וֹן סָֽתֶר׃
Better to live in a corner of the roof than in a house shared with a quarrelsome wife.[^10]
ט֗וֹב שֶׁ֥בֶת עַל־פִּנַּת־גָּ֑ג מֵאֵ֥שֶׁת *מדונים **מִ֝דְיָנִ֗ים וּבֵ֥ית חָֽבֶר׃
Like cold water to a weary soul is good news from a distant land.
מַ֣יִם קָ֭רִים עַל־נֶ֣פֶשׁ עֲיֵפָ֑ה וּשְׁמוּעָ֥ה ט֝וֹבָ֗ה מֵאֶ֥רֶץ מֶרְחָֽק׃
Like a muddied spring or a polluted fountain is a righteous person[^11] who gives way before the wicked.
מַעְיָ֣ן נִ֭רְפָּשׂ וּמָק֣וֹר מָשְׁחָ֑ת צַ֝דִּ֗יק מָ֣ט לִפְנֵֽי־רָשָֽׁע׃
It is not good to eat much honey, nor is it glorious to seek one's own glory.[^12]
אָ֘כֹ֤ל דְּבַ֣שׁ הַרְבּ֣וֹת לֹּא־ט֑וֹב וְחֵ֖קֶר כְּבֹדָ֣ם כָּבֽוֹד׃
Like a city broken into and left without walls is a person who has no control over his spirit.
עִ֣יר פְּ֭רוּצָה אֵ֣ין חוֹמָ֑ה אִ֝֗ישׁ אֲשֶׁ֤ר אֵ֖ין מַעְצָ֣ר לְרוּחֽוֹ׃

n.1: A new collection begins here (chapters 25–29). Hezekiah reigned more than two centuries after Solomon (2 Kings 18–20).
n.2: Hebrew *rasha*: one who is guilty of wrong (see 2:22).
n.3: Or "What your eyes have seen, (8) do not bring hastily to court". Compare Luke 14:8–10.
n.4: Hebrew *yechassedkha*, from the verb related to *chesed*, "disgrace" (14:34).
n.5: Literally "on its wheels", probably "at the right time" or "in the right way".
n.6: Hebrew *neter*, natron or soda, which fizzes when vinegar is poured on it.
n.7: Literally "the one who hates you".
n.8: *LORD*: God's personal name, Hebrew YHWH, written "the LORD" in capitals as in most English Bibles.
n.9: Romans 12:20 quotes verses 21–22.
n.10: The verse repeats 21:9.
n.11: Hebrew *tsaddiq*: one who does what is right (see 2:20).
n.12: The Hebrew of this line is difficult. Literally "and searching out their glory is glory". The translation carries over the "not" of the first line.

v: Like snow in summer and like rain at harvest, so honor is not fitting for a fool.[^1]
כַּשֶּׁ֤לֶג ׀ בַּקַּ֗יִץ וְכַמָּטָ֥ר בַּקָּצִ֑יר כֵּ֤ן לֹא־נָאוֶ֖ה לִכְסִ֣יל כָּבֽוֹד׃
Like a sparrow flitting, like a swallow flying, so an undeserved curse comes home to the one who utters it.[^2]
כַּצִּפּ֣וֹר לָ֭נוּד כַּדְּר֣וֹר לָע֑וּף כֵּ֥ן קִֽלְלַ֥ת חִ֝נָּ֗ם *לא **ל֣וֹ תָבֹֽא׃
A whip for the horse, a bridle for the donkey, and a rod for the backs of fools.
שׁ֣וֹט לַ֭סּוּס מֶ֣תֶג לַחֲמ֑וֹר וְ֝שֵׁ֗בֶט לְגֵ֣ו כְּסִילִֽים׃
Do not answer a fool according to his folly,[^3] or you will be like him yourself.
אַל־תַּ֣עַן כְּ֭סִיל כְּאִוַּלְתּ֑וֹ פֶּֽן־תִּשְׁוֶה־לּ֥וֹ גַם־אָֽתָּה׃
Answer a fool according to his folly, or he will be wise in his own eyes.[^4]
עֲנֵ֣ה כְ֭סִיל כְּאִוַּלְתּ֑וֹ פֶּן־יִהְיֶ֖ה חָכָ֣ם בְּעֵינָֽיו׃
Whoever sends a message by the hand of a fool cuts off his own feet and drinks violence.
מְקַצֶּ֣ה רַ֭גְלַיִם חָמָ֣ס שֹׁתֶ֑ה שֹׁלֵ֖חַ דְּבָרִ֣ים בְּיַד־כְּסִֽיל׃
Like the legs of a lame person, which hang useless, is a proverb in the mouth of fools.
דַּלְי֣וּ שֹׁ֭קַיִם מִפִּסֵּ֑חַ וּ֝מָשָׁ֗ל בְּפִ֣י כְסִילִֽים׃
Like tying a stone in a sling[^5] is giving honor to a fool.
כִּצְר֣וֹר אֶ֭בֶן בְּמַרְגֵּמָ֑ה כֵּן־נוֹתֵ֖ן לִכְסִ֣יל כָּבֽוֹד׃
Like a thorn that gets into the hand of a drunkard is a proverb in the mouth of fools.
ח֭וֹחַ עָלָ֣ה בְיַד־שִׁכּ֑וֹר וּ֝מָשָׁ֗ל בְּפִ֣י כְסִילִֽים׃
Like an archer who wounds everyone is one who hires a fool or hires passersby.[^6]
רַ֥ב מְחֽוֹלֵֽל־כֹּ֑ל וְשֹׂכֵ֥ר כְּ֝סִ֗יל וְשֹׂכֵ֥ר עֹבְרִֽים׃
Like a dog that returns to its vomit is a fool who repeats his folly.[^7]
כְּ֭כֶלֶב שָׁ֣ב עַל־קֵא֑וֹ כְּ֝סִ֗יל שׁוֹנֶ֥ה בְאִוַּלְתּֽוֹ׃
Do you see a person wise in his own eyes? There is more hope for a fool than for him.
רָאִ֗יתָ אִ֭ישׁ חָכָ֣ם בְּעֵינָ֑יו תִּקְוָ֖ה לִכְסִ֣יל מִמֶּֽנּוּ׃
The lazy person[^8] says, "There is a lion in the road! A lion in the streets!"[^9]
אָמַ֣ר עָ֭צֵל שַׁ֣חַל בַּדָּ֑רֶךְ אֲ֝רִ֗י בֵּ֣ין הָרְחֹבֽוֹת׃
As a door turns on its hinges, so the lazy person turns on his bed.
הַ֭דֶּלֶת תִּסּ֣וֹב עַל־צִירָ֑הּ וְ֝עָצֵ֗ל עַל־מִטָּתֽוֹ׃
The lazy person buries his hand in the dish; he is too tired to bring it back to his mouth.[^10]
טָ֘מַ֤ן עָצֵ֣ל יָ֭דוֹ בַּצַּלָּ֑חַת נִ֝לְאָ֗ה לַֽהֲשִׁיבָ֥הּ אֶל־פִּֽיו׃
The lazy person is wiser in his own eyes than seven people who answer sensibly.
חָכָ֣ם עָצֵ֣ל בְּעֵינָ֑יו מִ֝שִּׁבְעָ֗ה מְשִׁ֣יבֵי טָֽעַם׃
Like one who grabs a dog by the ears is a passerby who meddles[^11] in a quarrel not his own.
מַחֲזִ֥יק בְּאָזְנֵי־כָ֑לֶב עֹבֵ֥ר מִ֝תְעַבֵּ֗ר עַל־רִ֥יב לֹּֽא־לֽוֹ׃
Like a madman who shoots flaming arrows, arrows and death,
כְּֽ֭מִתְלַהְלֵהַּ הַיֹּרֶ֥ה זִקִּ֗ים חִצִּ֥ים וָמָֽוֶת׃
so is the man who deceives his neighbor and says, "I was only joking!"
כֵּֽן־אִ֭ישׁ רִמָּ֣ה אֶת־רֵעֵ֑הוּ וְ֝אָמַ֗ר הֲ‍ֽלֹא־מְשַׂחֵ֥ק אָֽנִי׃
Without wood a fire goes out, and without a gossip[^12] a quarrel dies down.
בְּאֶ֣פֶס עֵ֭צִים תִּכְבֶּה־אֵ֑שׁ וּבְאֵ֥ין נִ֝רְגָּ֗ן יִשְׁתֹּ֥ק מָדֽוֹן׃
As charcoal to embers and wood to fire, so is a quarrelsome man for kindling strife.
פֶּחָ֣ם לְ֭גֶחָלִים וְעֵצִ֣ים לְאֵ֑שׁ וְאִ֥ישׁ *מדונים **מִ֝דְיָנִ֗ים לְחַרְחַר־רִֽיב׃ פ
The words of a gossip are like tasty morsels; they go down into the inner parts of the body.[^13]
דִּבְרֵ֣י נִ֭רְגָּן כְּמִֽתְלַהֲמִ֑ים וְ֝הֵ֗ם יָרְד֥וּ חַדְרֵי־בָֽטֶן׃
Like glaze[^14] coating an earthenware pot are burning lips with an evil heart.
כֶּ֣סֶף סִ֭יגִים מְצֻפֶּ֣ה עַל־חָ֑רֶשׂ שְׂפָתַ֖יִם דֹּלְקִ֣ים וְלֶב־רָֽע׃
Whoever hates disguises it with his lips, but inside he harbors deceit.
*בשפתו **בִּ֭שְׂפָתָיו יִנָּכֵ֣ר שׂוֹנֵ֑א וּ֝בְקִרְבּ֗וֹ יָשִׁ֥ית מִרְמָֽה׃
When he speaks graciously, do not believe him, for seven detestable things[^15] are in his heart.
כִּֽי־יְחַנֵּ֣ן ק֭וֹלוֹ אַל־תַּֽאֲמֶן־בּ֑וֹ כִּ֤י שֶׁ֖בַע תּוֹעֵב֣וֹת בְּלִבּֽוֹ׃
His hatred may be covered by deception, but his evil will be exposed in the assembly.
תִּכַּסֶּ֣ה שִׂ֭נְאָה בְּמַשָּׁא֑וֹן תִּגָּלֶ֖ה רָעָת֣וֹ בְקָהָֽל׃
Whoever digs a pit will fall into it, and a stone will come back on the one who rolls it.
כֹּֽרֶה־שַּׁ֭חַת בָּ֣הּ יִפֹּ֑ל וְגֹ֥לֵ֥ל אֶ֝בֶן אֵלָ֥יו תָּשֽׁוּב׃
A lying tongue hates those it crushes,[^16] and a flattering mouth works ruin.
לְֽשׁוֹן־שֶׁ֭קֶר יִשְׂנָ֣א דַכָּ֑יו וּפֶ֥ה חָ֝לָ֗ק יַעֲשֶׂ֥ה מִדְחֶֽה׃

n.1: Hebrew *kesil*, the most common word for "fool" in Proverbs: someone dull and self-satisfied who does not want to learn (see 1:22). Throughout verses 1–12.
n.2: Literally "comes to him", probably the one who utters it. The Hebrew text is written "does not come", which gives the sense "so an undeserved curse does not land".
n.3: Hebrew *iwwelet*, "folly", the word related to *ewil*, "fool" (see 1:7). Also in verses 5 and 11.
n.4: Verses 4 and 5 are set side by side, giving opposite advice.
n.5: Or "Like a bag of precious stones in a heap of stones".
n.6: The Hebrew of this verse is very uncertain. Literally "Much (or 'An archer', or 'A master') wounding (or 'producing') all, and one who hires a fool and one who hires passersby".
n.7: 2 Peter 2:22 quotes the first line.
n.8: Hebrew *atsel*, traditionally "sluggard" (see 6:6). Also in verses 14–16.
n.9: Two different Hebrew words for "lion". Compare 22:13.
n.10: Compare 19:24.
n.11: Hebrew *mit'abber*, usually "becomes enraged"; here probably "gets involved".
n.12: Hebrew *nirgan*, "whisperer", as in 16:28. Also in verse 22.
n.13: The verse repeats 18:8.
n.14: The Hebrew vowel points read "silver of dross". The same consonants, divided into words differently, can be read "like glaze", a word known from other ancient languages.
n.15: Hebrew *to'evot*, plural of *to'evah*, "something loathsome" (see 3:32).
n.16: Literally "hates its crushed ones". The meaning is uncertain.

v: Do not boast about tomorrow, for you do not know what a day may bring.
אַֽל־תִּ֭תְהַלֵּל בְּי֣וֹם מָחָ֑ר כִּ֤י לֹא־תֵ֝דַ֗ע מַה־יֵּ֥לֶד יֽוֹם׃
Let a stranger praise you, and not your own mouth, an outsider,[^1] and not your own lips.
יְהַלֶּלְךָ֣ זָ֣ר וְלֹא־פִ֑יךָ נָ֝כְרִ֗י וְאַל־שְׂפָתֶֽיךָ׃
A stone is heavy and sand is weighty, but a fool's provocation is heavier than both.[^2]
כֹּֽבֶד־אֶ֭בֶן וְנֵ֣טֶל הַח֑וֹל וְכַ֥עַס אֱ֝וִ֗יל כָּבֵ֥ד מִשְּׁנֵיהֶֽם׃
Wrath is cruel and anger is a flood, but who can stand before jealousy?
אַכְזְרִיּ֣וּת חֵ֭מָה וְשֶׁ֣טֶף אָ֑ף וּמִ֥י יַ֝עֲמֹד לִפְנֵ֥י קִנְאָֽה׃
Better open correction than hidden love.
ט֭וֹבָה תּוֹכַ֣חַת מְגֻלָּ֑ה מֵֽאַהֲבָ֥ה מְסֻתָּֽרֶת׃
Wounds from a friend can be trusted, but the kisses of an enemy are lavish.[^3]
נֶ֭אֱמָנִים פִּצְעֵ֣י אוֹהֵ֑ב וְ֝נַעְתָּר֗וֹת נְשִׁיק֥וֹת שׂוֹנֵֽא׃
One who is full tramples on honey, but to one who is hungry everything bitter is sweet.
נֶ֣פֶשׁ שְׂ֭בֵעָה תָּב֣וּס נֹ֑פֶת וְנֶ֥פֶשׁ רְ֝עֵבָ֗ה כָּל־מַ֥ר מָתֽוֹק׃
Like a bird that strays from its nest is a man who strays from his home.
כְּ֭צִפּוֹר נוֹדֶ֣דֶת מִן־קִנָּ֑הּ כֵּֽן־אִ֝֗ישׁ נוֹדֵ֥ד מִמְּקוֹמֽוֹ׃
Oil and incense make the heart glad, and the sweetness of a friend comes from heartfelt advice.[^4]
שֶׁ֣מֶן וּ֭קְטֹרֶת יְשַׂמַּֽח־לֵ֑ב וּמֶ֥תֶק רֵ֝עֵ֗הוּ מֵֽעֲצַת־נָֽפֶשׁ׃
Do not abandon your friend or your father's friend, and do not go to your brother's house on the day of your disaster. Better a neighbor nearby than a brother far away.
רֵ֥עֲךָ֨ *ורעה **וְרֵ֪עַ אָבִ֡יךָ אַֽל־תַּעֲזֹ֗ב וּבֵ֥ית אָחִ֗יךָ אַל־תָּ֭בוֹא בְּי֣וֹם אֵידֶ֑ךָ ט֥וֹב שָׁכֵ֥ן קָ֝ר֗וֹב מֵאָ֥ח רָחֽוֹק׃
Be wise, my son, and make my heart glad, so that I can answer anyone who taunts me.
חֲכַ֣ם בְּ֭נִי וְשַׂמַּ֣ח לִבִּ֑י וְאָשִׁ֖יבָה חֹרְפִ֣י דָבָֽר׃
The prudent[^5] sees danger and hides himself; the simple[^6] go on and pay for it.[^7]
עָר֤וּם רָאָ֣ה רָעָ֣ה נִסְתָּ֑ר פְּ֝תָאיִ֗ם עָבְר֥וּ נֶעֱנָֽשׁוּ׃
Take the garment of one who puts up security for a stranger; hold it in pledge for a foreign woman.[^8]
קַח־בִּ֭גְדוֹ כִּי־עָ֣רַב זָ֑ר וּבְעַ֖ד נָכְרִיָּ֣ה חַבְלֵֽהוּ׃
Whoever blesses his neighbor with a loud voice early in the morning, it will be counted to him as a curse.
מְבָ֘רֵ֤ךְ רֵעֵ֨הוּ ׀ בְּק֣וֹל גָּ֭דוֹל בַּבֹּ֣קֶר הַשְׁכֵּ֑ים קְ֝לָלָ֗ה תֵּחָ֥שֶׁב לֽוֹ׃
A constant dripping on a rainy day and a quarrelsome wife are alike;
דֶּ֣לֶף ט֭[t]וֹרֵד בְּי֣וֹם סַגְרִ֑יר וְאֵ֥שֶׁת *מדונים **מִ֝דְיָנִ֗ים נִשְׁתָּוָֽה׃
whoever restrains her restrains the wind or grasps oil with his right hand.[^9]
צֹפְנֶ֥יהָ צָֽפַן־ר֑וּחַ וְשֶׁ֖מֶן יְמִינ֣וֹ יִקְרָֽא׃
As iron sharpens iron, so one person sharpens another.[^10]
בַּרְזֶ֣ל בְּבַרְזֶ֣ל יָ֑חַד וְ֝אִ֗ישׁ יַ֣חַד פְּנֵֽי־רֵעֵֽהוּ׃
Whoever tends a fig tree will eat its fruit, and whoever looks after his master will be honored.
נֹצֵ֣ר תְּ֭אֵנָה יֹאכַ֣ל פִּרְיָ֑הּ וְשֹׁמֵ֖ר אֲדֹנָ֣יו יְכֻבָּֽד׃
As water reflects the face, so the heart reflects the person.[^11]
כַּ֭מַּיִם הַפָּנִ֣ים לַפָּנִ֑ים כֵּ֤ן לֵֽב־הָ֝אָדָ֗ם לָאָדָֽם׃
Sheol and Abaddon[^12] are never satisfied, and human eyes are never satisfied.
שְׁא֣וֹל *ואבדה **וַ֭אֲבַדּוֹ לֹ֣א תִשְׂבַּ֑עְנָה וְעֵינֵ֥י הָ֝אָדָ֗ם לֹ֣א תִשְׂבַּֽעְנָה׃
The crucible is for silver and the furnace for gold, and a person is tested by the praise he receives.[^13]
מַצְרֵ֣ף לַ֭כֶּסֶף וְכ֣וּר לַזָּהָ֑ב וְ֝אִ֗ישׁ לְפִ֣י מַהֲלָלֽוֹ׃
Even if you pound a fool[^14] in a mortar, with a pestle among the grain, his folly will not leave him.
אִ֥ם תִּכְתּֽוֹשׁ־אֶת־הָאֱוִ֨יל ׀ בַּֽמַּכְתֵּ֡שׁ בְּת֣וֹךְ הָ֭רִיפוֹת בַּֽעֱלִ֑י לֹא־תָס֥וּר מֵ֝עָלָ֗יו אִוַּלְתּֽוֹ׃ פ
Know well the condition of your flocks; give careful attention to your herds,
יָדֹ֣עַ תֵּ֭דַע פְּנֵ֣י צֹאנֶ֑ךָ שִׁ֥ית לִ֝בְּךָ֗ לַעֲדָרִֽים׃
for riches do not last forever, and does a crown last for all generations?
כִּ֤י לֹ֣א לְעוֹלָ֣ם חֹ֑סֶן וְאִם־נֵ֝֗זֶר לְד֣וֹר *דור **וָדֽוֹר׃
When the grass is gone and the new growth appears, and the plants of the hills are gathered in,
גָּלָ֣ה חָ֭צִיר וְנִרְאָה־דֶ֑שֶׁא וְ֝נֶאֶסְפ֗וּ עִשְּׂב֥וֹת הָרִֽים׃
the lambs will provide your clothing, and the goats the price of a field,
כְּבָשִׂ֥ים לִלְבוּשֶׁ֑ךָ וּמְחִ֥יר שָׂ֝דֶ֗ה עַתּוּדִֽים׃
and there will be enough goats' milk for your food, for the food of your household, and to keep your servant girls alive.
וְדֵ֤י ׀ חֲלֵ֬ב עִזִּ֗ים לְֽ֭לַחְמְךָ לְלֶ֣חֶם בֵּיתֶ֑ךָ וְ֝חַיִּ֗ים לְנַעֲרוֹתֶֽיךָ׃

n.1: Hebrew *zar* and *nokhri*, the masculine forms of the words used for the "strange woman" and the "foreign woman" (2:16).
n.2: Hebrew *ewil*, the morally perverse, stubborn fool (see 1:7).
n.3: Hebrew *na'tarot*, perhaps "many, lavish", or "deceitful".
n.4: The Hebrew of this line is uncertain. Literally "and the sweetness of his friend from the advice of the soul". Or "and the sweetness of a friend is better than one's own advice".
n.5: Hebrew *arum*, "shrewd, prudent" (see 1:4).
n.6: Hebrew *peta'im*, plural of *peti*: naive, inexperienced people, easily led (see 1:4).
n.7: The verse repeats 22:3.
n.8: Hebrew *nokhriyyah*, "foreign woman" (see 2:16). The verse repeats 20:16.
n.9: The Hebrew of this verse is obscure. Literally "Those who hide her hide wind, and oil his right hand meets".
n.10: Literally "so a man sharpens the face of his friend".
n.11: Literally "As in water face to face, so the heart of a person to a person". This may mean that a person's heart shows what he is, or that one sees oneself in another's heart.
n.12: Hebrew *Sheol*, the realm of the dead, and *Abaddon*, "Destruction", another name for it (see 15:11).
n.13: Literally "and a man according to his praise". It may mean that a person is tested by how he takes praise, or known by what he praises.
n.14: Hebrew *ewil*, as in verse 3. *Folly* is *iwwelet*, the related word.

v: The wicked[^1] flee when no one pursues, but the righteous[^2] are as bold as a lion.
נָ֣סוּ וְאֵין־רֹדֵ֣ף רָשָׁ֑ע וְ֝צַדִּיקִ֗ים כִּכְפִ֥יר יִבְטָֽח׃
When a land rebels, it has many rulers, but through a person who understands and knows, its stability lasts.[^3]
בְּפֶ֣שַֽׁע אֶ֭רֶץ רַבִּ֣ים שָׂרֶ֑יהָ וּבְאָדָ֥ם מֵבִ֥ין יֹ֝דֵ֗עַ כֵּ֣ן יַאֲרִֽיךְ׃
A poor man who oppresses the poor is like a driving rain that leaves no food.
גּ[t]בֶר[t] רָ֭שׁ וְעֹשֵׁ֣ק דַּלִּ֑ים מָטָ֥ר סֹ֝חֵ֗ף וְאֵ֣ין לָֽחֶם׃
Those who abandon the law[^4] praise the wicked, but those who keep the law fight against them.
עֹזְבֵ֣י ת֭וֹרָה יְהַֽלְל֣וּ רָשָׁ֑ע וְשֹׁמְרֵ֥י ת֝וֹרָ֗ה יִתְגָּ֥רוּ בָֽם׃ פ
Evil people do not understand justice, but those who seek the LORD[^5] understand everything.
אַנְשֵׁי־רָ֭ע לֹא־יָבִ֣ינוּ מִשְׁפָּ֑ט וּמְבַקְשֵׁ֥י יְ֝הוָ֗ה יָבִ֥ינוּ כֹֽל׃
Better a poor person who walks in integrity than one whose ways are crooked,[^6] even if he is rich.
טֽוֹב־רָ֭שׁ הוֹלֵ֣ךְ בְּתֻמּ֑וֹ מֵעִקֵּ֥שׁ דְּ֝רָכַ֗יִם וְה֣וּא עָשִֽׁיר׃
Whoever keeps the law is a discerning son, but a companion of gluttons shames his father.
נוֹצֵ֣ר תּ֭וֹרָה בֵּ֣ן מֵבִ֑ין וְרֹעֶ֥[t]ה זֽ֝וֹלְלִ֗ים יַכְלִ֥ים אָבִֽיו׃
Whoever increases his wealth by interest and profit[^7] gathers it for one who is kind to the poor.
מַרְבֶּ֣ה ה֭וֹנוֹ בְּנֶ֣שֶׁךְ *ובתרבית **וְתַרְבִּ֑ית לְחוֹנֵ֖ן דַּלִּ֣ים יִקְבְּצֶֽנּוּ׃
Whoever turns his ear away from hearing the law, even his prayer is detestable.
מֵסִ֣יר אָ֭זְנוֹ מִשְּׁמֹ֣עַ תּוֹרָ֑ה גַּ֥ם תְּ֝פִלָּת֗וֹ תּוֹעֵבָֽה׃
Whoever leads the upright astray into an evil way will fall into his own pit, but the blameless will inherit good.
מַשְׁגֶּ֤ה יְשָׁרִ֨ים ׀ בְּדֶ֥רֶךְ רָ֗ע בִּשְׁחוּת֥וֹ הֽוּא־יִפּ֑וֹל וּ֝תְמִימִ֗ים יִנְחֲלוּ־טֽוֹב׃
A rich man is wise in his own eyes, but a poor man who is discerning sees through him.
חָכָ֣ם בְּ֭עֵינָיו אִ֣ישׁ עָשִׁ֑יר וְדַ֖ל מֵבִ֣ין יַחְקְרֶֽנּוּ׃
When the righteous triumph, there is great glory, but when the wicked rise, people hide.[^8]
בַּעֲלֹ֣ץ צַ֭דִּיקִים רַבָּ֣ה תִפְאָ֑רֶת וּבְק֥וּם רְ֝שָׁעִ֗ים יְחֻפַּ֥שׂ אָדָֽם׃
Whoever covers his offenses will not prosper, but whoever confesses and abandons them will find mercy.
מְכַסֶּ֣ה פְ֭שָׁעָיו לֹ֣א יַצְלִ֑יחַ וּמוֹדֶ֖ה וְעֹזֵ֣ב יְרֻחָֽם׃
Happy[^9] is the one who is always reverent,[^10] but whoever hardens his heart will fall into trouble.
אַשְׁרֵ֣י אָ֭דָם מְפַחֵ֣ד תָּמִ֑יד וּמַקְשֶׁ֥ה לִ֝בּ֗וֹ יִפּ֥וֹל בְּרָעָֽה׃
Like a roaring lion or a charging bear is a wicked ruler over a poor people.
אֲרִי־נֹ֭הֵם וְדֹ֣ב שׁוֹקֵ֑ק מֹשֵׁ֥ל רָ֝שָׁ֗ע עַ֣ל עַם־דָּֽל׃
A ruler who lacks insight[^11] is a great oppressor, but whoever hates unjust gain will live long.
נָגִ֗יד חֲסַ֣ר תְּ֭בוּנוֹת וְרַ֥ב מַעֲשַׁקּ֑וֹת *שנאי **שֹׂ֥נֵא בֶ֝֗צַע יַאֲרִ֥יךְ יָמִֽים׃ פ
A man burdened with someone's blood will be a fugitive until the Pit;[^12] let no one hold him back.
אָ֭דָם עָשֻׁ֣ק בְּדַם־נָפֶשׁ[c] עַד־בּ֥וֹר יָ֝נ֗וּס אַל־יִתְמְכוּ־בֽוֹ׃
Whoever walks blamelessly will be kept safe, but whoever is crooked in his ways will fall all at once.
הוֹלֵ֣ךְ תָּ֭מִים יִוָּשֵׁ֑עַ וְנֶעְקַ֥שׁ דְּ֝רָכַ֗יִם יִפּ֥וֹל בְּאֶחָֽת׃
Whoever works his land will have plenty of bread, but whoever chases worthless things will have plenty of poverty.
עֹבֵ֣ד אַ֭דְמָתוֹ יִֽשְׂבַּֽע־לָ֑חֶם וּמְרַדֵּ֥ף רֵ֝קִ֗ים יִֽשְׂבַּֽע־רִֽישׁ׃
A faithful person will have many blessings, but whoever hurries to get rich will not go unpunished.
אִ֣ישׁ אֱ֭מוּנוֹת רַב־בְּרָכ֑וֹת וְאָ֥ץ לְ֝הַעֲשִׁ֗יר לֹ֣א יִנָּקֶֽה׃
Showing partiality is not good, yet for a piece of bread a man will do wrong.
הַֽכֵּר־פָּנִ֥ים לֹא־ט֑וֹב וְעַל־פַּת־לֶ֝֗חֶם יִפְשַׁע־גָּֽבֶר׃
A stingy man[^13] hurries after wealth and does not know that poverty will come upon him.
נִֽבֳהָֽ[m]ל לַה֗וֹן אִ֭ישׁ רַ֣ע עָ֑יִן וְלֹֽא־יֵ֝דַע כִּי־חֶ֥סֶר יְבֹאֶֽנּוּ׃
Whoever corrects someone will in the end[^14] find more favor than one who flatters with his tongue.
מ֘וֹכִ֤יחַ אָדָ֣ם אַ֭חֲרַי חֵ֣ן יִמְצָ֑א מִֽמַּחֲלִ֥יק לָשֽׁוֹן׃
Whoever robs his father or his mother and says, "It is no offense," is a companion of a destroyer.
גּוֹזֵ֤ל ׀ אָ֘בִ֤יו וְאִמּ֗וֹ וְאֹמֵ֥ר אֵֽין־פָּ֑שַׁע חָבֵ֥ר ה֝֗וּא לְאִ֣ישׁ מַשְׁחִֽית׃
The greedy person[^15] stirs up strife, but whoever trusts in the LORD will prosper.
רְחַב־נֶ֭פֶשׁ יְגָרֶ֣ה מָד֑וֹן וּבוֹטֵ֖חַ עַל־יְהוָ֣ה יְדֻשָּֽׁן׃
Whoever trusts in his own heart is a fool,[^16] but whoever walks in wisdom will be kept safe.
בּוֹטֵ֣חַ בְּ֭לִבּוֹ ה֣וּא כְסִ֑יל וְהוֹלֵ֥ךְ בְּ֝חָכְמָ֗ה ה֣וּא יִמָּלֵֽט׃
Whoever gives to the poor will not lack, but whoever shuts his eyes will receive many curses.
נוֹתֵ֣ן לָ֭רָשׁ אֵ֣ין מַחְס֑וֹר וּמַעְלִ֥ים עֵ֝ינָ֗יו רַב־מְאֵרֽוֹת׃
When the wicked rise, people hide, but when they perish, the righteous increase.
בְּק֣וּם רְ֭שָׁעִים יִסָּתֵ֣ר אָדָ֑ם וּ֝בְאָבְדָ֗ם יִרְבּ֥וּ צַדִּיקִֽים׃

n.1: Hebrew *rasha*: one who is guilty of wrong (see 2:22).
n.2: Hebrew *tsaddiqim*, plural of *tsaddiq*: those who do what is right (see 2:20).
n.3: The Hebrew of this line is difficult. Literally "but by a person who understands, who knows, so it lasts long".
n.4: Hebrew *torah*, "instruction", here probably God's law. Also in verses 7 and 9.
n.5: *LORD*: God's personal name, Hebrew YHWH, written "the LORD" in capitals as in most English Bibles.
n.6: Literally "crooked of two ways", perhaps double-dealing. Also in verse 18. Compare 19:1.
n.7: Lending at interest to a fellow Israelite was forbidden (Leviticus 25:36–37).
n.8: Literally "a person must be searched for".
n.9: Hebrew *ashrei*: happy, fortunate; traditionally "blessed".
n.10: Literally "who fears always", that is, fears God, or fears doing wrong.
n.11: Literally "lacking insights". Hebrew *tevunot*, plural of *tevunah* (see 2:2).
n.12: That is, until death. Hebrew *bor*, "pit", as in 1:12.
n.13: Literally "A man with an evil eye".
n.14: Hebrew *acharai*, literally "after me", probably "afterward".
n.15: Literally "One who is wide of appetite (*nephesh*)".
n.16: Hebrew *kesil* (see 1:22).

v: Whoever is often corrected yet stays stiff-necked will suddenly be broken, and there will be no healing.
אִ֣ישׁ תּ֭וֹכָחוֹת מַקְשֶׁה־עֹ֑רֶף פֶּ֥תַע יִ֝שָּׁבֵ֗ר וְאֵ֣ין מַרְפֵּֽא׃
When the righteous[^1] increase, the people rejoice, but when the wicked[^2] rule, the people groan.
בִּרְב֣וֹת צַ֭דִּיקִים יִשְׂמַ֣ח הָעָ֑ם וּבִמְשֹׁ֥ל רָ֝שָׁ֗ע יֵאָ֥נַֽח עָֽם׃
A man who loves wisdom makes his father glad, but a companion of prostitutes squanders his wealth.
אִֽישׁ־אֹהֵ֣ב חָ֭כְמָה יְשַׂמַּ֣ח אָבִ֑יו וְרֹעֶ֥ה ז֝וֹנ֗וֹת יְאַבֶּד־הֽוֹן׃
By justice a king gives a land stability, but a man who exacts contributions[^3] tears it down.
מֶ֗לֶךְ בְּ֭מִשְׁפָּט יַעֲמִ֣יד אָ֑רֶץ וְאִ֖ישׁ תְּרוּמ֣וֹת יֶֽהֶרְסֶֽנָּה׃
A man who flatters his neighbor is spreading a net for his feet.[^4]
גֶּ֭בֶר מַחֲלִ֣יק עַל־רֵעֵ֑הוּ רֶ֝֗שֶׁת פּוֹרֵ֥שׂ עַל־פְּעָמָֽיו׃
An evil man is snared by his own offense, but the righteous sings and rejoices.
בְּפֶ֤שַֽׁע אִ֣ישׁ רָ֣ע מוֹקֵ֑שׁ וְ֝צַדִּ֗יק יָר֥וּן וְשָׂמֵֽחַ׃
The righteous knows the rights of the poor; the wicked has no such understanding.[^5]
יֹדֵ֣עַ צַ֭דִּיק דִּ֣ין דַּלִּ֑ים רָ֝שָׁ֗ע לֹא־יָבִ֥ין דָּֽעַת׃
Mockers[^6] set a city aflame, but the wise turn away anger.
אַנְשֵׁ֣י לָ֭צוֹן יָפִ֣יחוּ קִרְיָ֑ה וַ֝חֲכָמִ֗ים יָשִׁ֥יבוּ אָֽף׃
If a wise man goes to court with a fool,[^7] the fool rages and laughs,[^8] and there is no peace.
אִֽישׁ־חָכָ֗ם נִ֭שְׁפָּט אֶת־אִ֣ישׁ אֱוִ֑יל וְרָגַ֥ז וְ֝שָׂחַ֗ק וְאֵ֣ין נָֽחַת׃
Bloodthirsty men hate the blameless, and as for the upright, they seek his life.[^9]
אַנְשֵׁ֣י דָ֭מִים יִשְׂנְאוּ־תָ֑ם וִֽ֝ישָׁרִ֗ים יְבַקְשׁ֥וּ נַפְשֽׁוֹ׃
A fool[^10] gives full vent to his anger,[^11] but a wise person quietly holds it back.
כָּל־ר֭וּחוֹ יוֹצִ֣יא כְסִ֑יל וְ֝חָכָ֗ם בְּאָח֥וֹר יְשַׁבְּחֶֽנָּה׃
If a ruler listens to lies, all his officials become wicked.
מֹ֭שֵׁל מַקְשִׁ֣יב עַל־דְּבַר־שָׁ֑קֶר כָּֽל־מְשָׁרְתָ֥יו רְשָׁעִֽים׃
The poor and the oppressor meet together; the LORD[^12] gives light to the eyes of both.[^13]
רָ֤שׁ וְאִ֣ישׁ תְּכָכִ֣ים נִפְגָּ֑שׁוּ מֵ֤אִיר־עֵינֵ֖י שְׁנֵיהֶ֣ם יְהוֽ͏ָה׃
If a king judges the poor with faithfulness, his throne will be established forever.
מֶ֤לֶךְ שׁוֹפֵ֣ט בֶּֽאֱמֶ֣ת דַּלִּ֑ים כִּ֝סְא֗וֹ לָעַ֥ד יִכּֽוֹן׃
The rod and correction give wisdom, but a child left to himself brings shame to his mother.
שֵׁ֣בֶט וְ֭תוֹכַחַת יִתֵּ֣ן חָכְמָ֑ה וְנַ֥עַר מְ֝שֻׁלָּ֗ח מֵבִ֥ישׁ אִמּֽוֹ׃
When the wicked increase, offense increases, but the righteous will see their downfall.
בִּרְב֣וֹת רְ֭שָׁעִים יִרְבֶּה־פָּ֑שַׁע וְ֝צַדִּיקִ֗ים בְּֽמַפַּלְתָּ֥ם יִרְאֽוּ׃
Discipline your son, and he will give you rest; he will bring delight to your soul.
יַסֵּ֣ר בִּ֭נְךָ וִֽינִיחֶ֑ךָ וְיִתֵּ֖ן מַעֲדַנִּ֣ים לְנַפְשֶֽׁךָ׃ פ
Where there is no vision,[^14] the people run wild, but whoever keeps the law[^15] is happy.[^16]
בְּאֵ֣ין חָ֭זוֹן יִפָּ֣רַֽע עָ֑ם וְשֹׁמֵ֖ר תּוֹרָ֣ה אַשְׁרֵֽהוּ׃
A servant cannot be disciplined by words alone; though he understands, he will not respond.
בִּ֭דְבָרִים לֹא־יִוָּ֣סֶר עָ֑בֶד כִּֽי־יָ֝בִ֗ין וְאֵ֣ין מַעֲנֶֽה׃
Do you see someone who is hasty in his words? There is more hope for a fool than for him.
חָזִ֗יתָ אִ֭ישׁ אָ֣ץ בִּדְבָרָ֑יו תִּקְוָ֖ה לִכְסִ֣יל מִמֶּֽנּוּ׃
If someone pampers his servant from youth, in the end it will bring grief.[^17]
מְפַנֵּ֣ק מִנֹּ֣עַר עַבְדּ֑וֹ וְ֝אַחֲרִית֗וֹ יִהְיֶ֥ה מָנֽוֹן׃
An angry man stirs up strife, and a hot-tempered man commits many offenses.
אִֽישׁ־אַ֭ף יְגָרֶ֣ה מָד֑וֹן וּבַ֖עַל חֵמָ֣ה רַב־פָּֽשַׁע׃
A person's pride will bring him low, but the lowly in spirit will gain honor.
גַּאֲוַ֣ת אָ֭דָם תַּשְׁפִּילֶ֑נּוּ וּשְׁפַל־ר֝֗וּחַ יִתְמֹ֥ךְ כָּבֽוֹד׃
Whoever is a partner with a thief hates his own life; he hears the curse but does not testify.[^18]
חוֹלֵ֣ק עִם־גַּ֭נָּב שׂוֹנֵ֣א נַּפְשׁ֑וֹ אָלָ֥ה יִ֝שְׁמַ֗ע וְלֹ֣א יַגִּֽיד׃
Fear of people sets a snare, but whoever trusts in the LORD is kept safe.
חֶרְדַּ֣ת אָ֭דָם יִתֵּ֣ן מוֹקֵ֑שׁ וּבוֹטֵ֖חַ בַּיהוָ֣ה יְשֻׂגָּֽב׃
Many seek the favor of a ruler, but justice for a person comes from the LORD.
רַ֭בִּים מְבַקְשִׁ֣ים פְּנֵי־מוֹשֵׁ֑ל וּ֝מֵיְהוָ֗ה מִשְׁפַּט־אִֽישׁ׃
An unjust man is detestable to the righteous, and one whose way is upright is detestable to the wicked.
תּוֹעֲבַ֣ת צַ֭דִּיקִים אִ֣ישׁ עָ֑וֶל וְתוֹעֲבַ֖ת רָשָׁ֣ע יְשַׁר־דָּֽרֶךְ׃ פ

n.1: Hebrew *tsaddiqim*, plural of *tsaddiq*: those who do what is right (see 2:20).
n.2: Hebrew *rasha*: one who is guilty of wrong (see 2:22).
n.3: Hebrew *terumot*, "contributions", perhaps heavy taxes or bribes.
n.4: Either his neighbor's feet or his own.
n.5: Literally "the wicked does not understand knowledge".
n.6: Literally "Men of mockery". Hebrew *latson*, from the same root as *lets*, "mocker" (see 1:22).
n.7: Hebrew *ewil*, the morally perverse, stubborn fool (see 1:7).
n.8: Or "whether the wise man is angry or laughs".
n.9: Literally "and the upright seek his life". This may mean that the upright care for the blameless person's life, or that the bloodthirsty seek the life of the upright.
n.10: Hebrew *kesil* (see 1:22). Also in verse 20.
n.11: Literally "brings out all his spirit (*ruach*)".
n.12: *LORD*: God's personal name, Hebrew YHWH, written "the LORD" in capitals as in most English Bibles.
n.13: Compare 22:2.
n.14: Hebrew *chazon*, a prophet's vision, revelation from God.
n.15: Hebrew *torah*, "instruction", here probably God's law.
n.16: Hebrew *ashrei*: happy, fortunate; traditionally "blessed".
n.17: Literally "and his end will be *manon*", a word found only here, of uncertain meaning: perhaps "grief", "insolence" or "an heir".
n.18: The *curse* is the public oath that called on witnesses to come forward (Leviticus 5:1).

v: The words of Agur son of Jakeh, the oracle.[^1] The man declares to Ithiel, to Ithiel and Ucal:[^2]
דִּבְרֵ֤י ׀ אָג֥וּר בִּן־יָקֶ֗ה הַמַּ֫שָּׂ֥א נְאֻ֣ם הַ֭גֶּבֶר לְאִֽיתִיאֵ֑ל לְאִ֖יתִיאֵ֣ל וְאֻכָֽל׃
Surely I am too stupid[^3] to be a man; I do not have human understanding.[^4]
כִּ֤י בַ֣עַר אָנֹכִ֣י מֵאִ֑ישׁ וְלֹֽא־בִינַ֖ת אָדָ֣ם לִֽי׃
I have not learned wisdom, nor do I have knowledge of the Holy One.[^5]
וְלֹֽא־לָמַ֥דְתִּי חָכְמָ֑ה וְדַ֖עַת קְדֹשִׁ֣ים אֵדָֽע׃

Who has gone up to heaven and come down? Who has gathered the wind in his fists? Who has wrapped up the waters in a cloak? Who has established all the ends of the earth? What is his name, and what is his son's name? Surely you know![^6]
מִ֤י עָלָֽה־שָׁמַ֨יִם ׀ וַיֵּרַ֡ד מִ֤י אָֽסַף־ר֨וּחַ ׀ בְּחָפְנָ֡יו מִ֤י צָֽרַר־מַ֨יִם ׀ בַּשִּׂמְלָ֗ה מִ֭י הֵקִ֣ים כָּל־אַפְסֵי־אָ֑רֶץ מַה־שְּׁמ֥וֹ וּמַֽה־שֶּׁם־בְּ֝נ֗וֹ כִּ֣י תֵדָֽע׃
Every word of God[^7] is refined; he is a shield to those who take refuge in him.
כָּל־אִמְּרַ֣ת אֱל֣וֹהַּ צְרוּפָ֑ה מָגֵ֥ן ה֝֗וּא לַֽחֹסִ֥ים בּֽוֹ׃
Do not add to his words, or he will rebuke you, and you will be found a liar.[^8]
אַל־תּ֥וֹסְףְּ עַל־דְּבָרָ֑יו פֶּן־יוֹכִ֖יחַ בְּךָ֣ וְנִכְזָֽבְתָּ׃ פ
Two things I ask of you; do not refuse me before I die:
שְׁ֭תַּיִם שָׁאַ֣לְתִּי מֵאִתָּ֑ךְ אַל־תִּמְנַ֥ע מִ֝מֶּ֗נִּי בְּטֶ֣רֶם אָמֽוּת׃
keep falsehood and lies far from me; give me neither poverty nor riches; feed me with the bread I need,[^9]
שָׁ֤וְא ׀ וּֽדְבַר־כָּזָ֡ב הַרְחֵ֬ק מִמֶּ֗נִּי רֵ֣אשׁ וָ֭עֹשֶׁר אַל־תִּֽתֶּן־לִ֑י הַ֝טְרִיפֵ֗נִי לֶ֣חֶם חֻקִּֽי׃
or I may become full and deny you and say, "Who is the LORD?"[^10] or I may become poor and steal, and profane the name of my God.
פֶּ֥ן אֶשְׂבַּ֨ע ׀ וְכִחַשְׁתִּי֮ וְאָמַ֗רְתִּי מִ֥י יְה֫וָ֥ה וּפֶֽן־אִוָּרֵ֥שׁ וְגָנַ֑בְתִּי וְ֝תָפַ֗שְׂתִּי שֵׁ֣ם אֱלֹהָֽי׃ פ
Do not slander a servant to his master, or he will curse you, and you will be held guilty.
אַל־תַּלְשֵׁ֣ן עֶ֭בֶד אֶל־*אדנו **אֲדֹנָ֑יו פֶּֽן־יְקַלֶּלְךָ֥ וְאָשָֽׁמְתָּ׃
There are those[^11] who curse their father and do not bless their mother.
דּ֭וֹר אָבִ֣יו יְקַלֵּ֑ל וְאֶת־אִ֝מּ֗וֹ לֹ֣א יְבָרֵֽךְ׃
There are those who are pure in their own eyes, yet are not washed of their filth.
דּ֭וֹר טָה֣וֹר בְּעֵינָ֑יו וּ֝מִצֹּאָת֗וֹ לֹ֣א רֻחָֽץ׃
There are those whose eyes are so haughty, whose eyelids are lifted high.
דּ֭וֹר מָה־רָמ֣וּ עֵינָ֑יו וְ֝עַפְעַפָּ֗יו יִנָּשֵֽׂאוּ׃
There are those whose teeth are swords, whose jaws are knives, to devour the poor from the earth and the needy from among humankind.
דּ֤וֹר ׀ חֲרָב֣וֹת שִׁנָּיו֮ וּֽמַאֲכָל֢וֹת מְֽתַלְּעֹ֫תָ֥יו לֶאֱכֹ֣ל עֲנִיִּ֣ים מֵאֶ֑רֶץ וְ֝אֶבְיוֹנִ֗ים מֵאָדָֽם׃ פ
The leech[^12] has two daughters: "Give! Give!" There are three things that are never satisfied, four that never say, "Enough!":[^13]
לַ֥עֲלוּקָ֨ה ׀ שְׁתֵּ֥י בָנוֹת֮ הַ֤ב ׀ הַ֥ב שָׁל֣וֹשׁ הֵ֭נָּה לֹ֣א תִשְׂבַּ֑עְנָה אַ֝רְבַּ֗ע לֹא־אָ֥מְרוּ הֽוֹן׃
Sheol,[^14] the barren womb, land that is never satisfied with water, and fire that never says, "Enough!"
שְׁאוֹל֮ וְעֹ֢צֶ֫ר רָ֥חַם אֶ֭רֶץ לֹא־שָׂ֣בְעָה מַּ֑יִם וְ֝אֵ֗שׁ לֹא־אָ֥מְרָה הֽוֹן׃
The eye that mocks a father and scorns obedience[^15] to a mother will be pecked out by the ravens of the valley and eaten by the young vultures.[^16]
עַ֤יִן ׀ תִּֽלְעַ֣ג לְאָב֮ וְתָב֢וּז לִֽיקֲּהַ֫ת־אֵ֥ם יִקְּר֥וּהָ עֹרְבֵי־נַ֑חַל וְֽיֹאכְל֥וּהָ בְנֵי־נָֽשֶׁר׃ פ
There are three things too wonderful for me, four that I do not understand:
שְׁלֹשָׁ֣ה הֵ֭מָּה נִפְלְא֣וּ מִמֶּ֑נִּי *וארבע **וְ֝אַרְבָּעָ֗ה לֹ֣א יְדַעְתִּֽים׃
the way of an eagle in the sky, the way of a snake on a rock, the way of a ship on the high seas, and the way of a man with a young woman.[^17]
דֶּ֤רֶךְ הַנֶּ֨שֶׁר ׀ בַּשָּׁמַיִם֮ דֶּ֥רֶךְ נָחָ֗שׁ עֲלֵ֫י צ֥וּר דֶּֽרֶךְ־אֳנִיָּ֥ה בְלֶב־יָ֑ם וְדֶ֖רֶךְ גֶּ֣בֶר בְּעַלְמָֽה׃
This is the way of an adulterous woman: she eats and wipes her mouth and says, "I have done nothing wrong."
כֵּ֤ן ׀ דֶּ֥רֶךְ אִשָּׁ֗ה מְנָ֫אָ֥פֶת אָ֭כְלָה וּמָ֣חֲתָה פִ֑יהָ וְ֝אָמְרָ֗ה לֹֽא־פָעַ֥לְתִּי אָֽוֶן׃ פ
Under three things the earth trembles, under four it cannot bear up:
תַּ֣חַת שָׁ֭לוֹשׁ רָ֣גְזָה אֶ֑רֶץ וְתַ֥חַת אַ֝רְבַּ֗ע לֹא־תוּכַ֥ל שְׂאֵֽת׃
a servant when he becomes king, a godless fool[^18] when he is filled with food,
תַּֽחַת־עֶ֭בֶד כִּ֣י יִמְל֑וֹךְ וְ֝נָבָ֗ל כִּ֣י יִֽשְׂבַּֽע־לָֽחֶם׃
an unloved woman when she gets a husband, and a servant girl when she takes the place of her mistress.
תַּ֣חַת שְׂ֭נוּאָה כִּ֣י תִבָּעֵ֑ל וְ֝שִׁפְחָ֗ה כִּֽי־תִירַ֥שׁ גְּבִרְתָּֽהּ׃ פ
Four things on earth are small, but they are exceedingly wise:
אַרְבָּ֣עָה הֵ֭ם קְטַנֵּי־אָ֑רֶץ וְ֝הֵ֗מָּה חֲכָמִ֥ים מְחֻכָּמִֽים׃
the ants are a people without strength, yet they store up their food in summer;
הַ֭נְּמָלִים עַ֣ם לֹא־עָ֑ז וַיָּכִ֖ינוּ בַקַּ֣יִץ לַחְמָֽם׃
the rock badgers[^19] are a people without power, yet they make their homes in the rocks;
שְׁ֭פַנִּים עַ֣ם לֹא־עָצ֑וּם וַיָּשִׂ֖ימוּ בַסֶּ֣לַע בֵּיתָֽם׃
the locusts have no king, yet they all go out in ranks;
מֶ֭לֶךְ אֵ֣ין לָאַרְבֶּ֑ה וַיֵּצֵ֖א חֹצֵ֣ץ כֻּלּֽוֹ׃
the lizard[^20] can be caught in the hand,[^21] yet it lives in kings' palaces.
שְׂ֭מָמִית בְּיָדַ֣יִם תְּתַפֵּ֑שׂ וְ֝הִ֗יא בְּהֵ֣יכְלֵי מֶֽלֶךְ׃ פ
There are three things that are stately in their stride, four that are stately in their walk:
שְׁלֹשָׁ֣ה הֵ֭מָּה מֵיטִ֣יבֵי צָ֑עַד וְ֝אַרְבָּעָ֗ה מֵיטִ֥בֵי לָֽכֶת׃
the lion, mightiest among beasts, which does not turn back before anything;
לַ֭יִשׁ גִּבּ֣וֹר בַּבְּהֵמָ֑ה וְלֹא־יָ֝שׁ֗וּב מִפְּנֵי־כֹֽל׃
the strutting rooster,[^22] or the male goat, and a king with his army around him.[^23]
זַרְזִ֣יר מָתְנַ֣יִם אוֹ־תָ֑יִשׁ וּ֝מֶ֗לֶךְ אַלְק֥וּם עִמּֽוֹ׃
If you have been foolish, exalting yourself, or if you have been scheming, put your hand over your mouth.
אִם־נָבַ֥לְתָּ בְהִתְנַשֵּׂ֑א וְאִם־זַ֝מּ֗וֹתָ יָ֣ד לְפֶֽה׃
For pressing milk produces curds, pressing the nose produces blood, and pressing anger produces strife.[^24]
כִּ֤י מִ֪יץ חָלָ֡ב י֘וֹצִ֤יא חֶמְאָ֗ה וּֽמִיץ־אַ֭ף י֣וֹצִיא דָ֑ם וּמִ֥יץ אַ֝פַּ֗יִם י֣וֹצִיא רִֽיב׃ פ

n.1: Or "of Massa", an Arabian tribe descended from Ishmael (Genesis 25:14); also in 31:1. Nothing more is known of Agur, and it is not clear where his words end. On the order of chapters 30–31 in the Septuagint, see the note on 24:23.
n.2: With different vowels and a different division of the words, "I am weary, O God; I am weary, O God, and I am worn out".
n.3: Hebrew *ba'ar*, "brutish", as in 12:1.
n.4: Hebrew *binah*, as in 1:2.
n.5: Literally "and the knowledge of the Holy One I know"; the "not" of the first line probably carries over. Or "yet I know the knowledge of the Holy One". *The Holy One* is Hebrew *qedoshim*, as in 9:10.
n.6: Or "if you know!"
n.7: Hebrew *Eloah*, a poetic form of *Elohim*, "God". The line is nearly the same as Psalm 18:31 (18:30 in most English Bibles) and 2 Samuel 22:31.
n.8: Compare Deuteronomy 4:2; 13:1 (12:32 in most English Bibles).
n.9: Literally "the bread of my portion".
n.10: *LORD*: God's personal name, Hebrew YHWH, written "the LORD" in capitals as in most English Bibles.
n.11: Literally "A generation", that is, a kind of people. Also in verses 12–14.
n.12: Hebrew *aluqah*, a word found only here, probably "leech".
n.13: The pattern "three … four" builds up to the last item in the list (compare 6:16). Also in verses 18, 21 and 29.
n.14: Hebrew *Sheol*, the realm of the dead.
n.15: Hebrew *yiqqahat*, a rare word, perhaps "obedience" (Genesis 49:10).
n.16: Or "young eagles". Hebrew *nesher*.
n.17: Hebrew *almah*, a young woman old enough to marry (Genesis 24:43; Isaiah 7:14).
n.18: Hebrew *nabal*: a senseless, godless person (see 17:7).
n.19: Hebrew *shefannim*, the rock hyrax, a small animal that lives among rocks (Psalm 104:18).
n.20: Hebrew *semamit*, probably a lizard or gecko; traditionally "spider".
n.22: Hebrew *zarzir motnayim*, literally "girded at the waist", an animal that cannot be identified with certainty: perhaps a rooster, a greyhound or a war horse.
n.23: Hebrew *alqum*, a word of uncertain meaning: perhaps "his army", or "against whom no one rises up".
n.24: In Hebrew *af*, "nose", and *appayim*, "anger" (literally "nostrils"), are the same word.

v: The words of King Lemuel, an oracle[^1] that his mother taught him.
דִּ֭בְרֵי לְמוּאֵ֣ל מֶ֑לֶךְ מַ֝שָּׂ֗א אֲ‍ֽשֶׁר־יִסְּרַ֥תּוּ אִמּֽוֹ׃
What, my son? What, son of my womb? What, son of my vows?[^2]
מַה־בְּ֭רִי וּמַֽה־בַּר־בִּטְנִ֑י וּ֝מֶה בַּר־נְדָרָֽי׃
Do not give your strength to women, your ways to those who destroy kings.
אַל־תִּתֵּ֣ן לַנָּשִׁ֣ים חֵילֶ֑ךָ וּ֝דְרָכֶ֗יךָ לַֽמְח֥וֹת מְלָכִֽין׃
It is not for kings, Lemuel, not for kings to drink wine, nor for rulers to ask, "Where is beer?"[^3]
אַ֤ל לַֽמְלָכִ֨ים ׀ לְֽמוֹאֵ֗ל אַ֣ל לַֽמְלָכִ֣ים שְׁתוֹ־יָ֑יִן וּ֝לְרוֹזְנִ֗ים *או **אֵ֣י שֵׁכָֽר׃
or they will drink and forget what has been decreed and pervert the rights of all the afflicted.
פֶּן־יִ֭שְׁתֶּה וְיִשְׁכַּ֣ח מְחֻקָּ֑ק וִֽ֝ישַׁנֶּה דִּ֣ין כָּל־בְּנֵי־עֹֽנִי׃
Give beer to one who is perishing, and wine to those who are bitter in soul.
תְּנוּ־שֵׁכָֽר לְאוֹבֵ֑ד וְ֝יַיִן לְמָ֣רֵי נָֽפֶשׁ׃
Let them drink and forget their poverty and remember their trouble no more.
יִ֭שְׁתֶּה וְיִשְׁכַּ֣ח רִישׁ֑וֹ וַ֝עֲמָל֗וֹ לֹ֣א יִזְכָּר־עֽוֹד׃
Open your mouth for those who cannot speak, for the rights of all who are destitute.[^4]
פְּתַח־פִּ֥יךָ לְאִלֵּ֑ם אֶל־דִּ֝֗ין כָּל־בְּנֵ֥י חֲלֽוֹף׃
Open your mouth, judge rightly, and defend the rights of the poor and needy.
פְּתַח־פִּ֥יךָ שְׁפָט־צֶ֑דֶק וְ֝דִ֗ין עָנִ֥י וְאֶבְיֽוֹן׃ פ
A capable wife,[^5] who can find? She is worth far more than coral.[^6]
אֵֽשֶׁת־חַ֭יִל מִ֣י יִמְצָ֑א וְרָחֹ֖ק מִפְּנִינִ֣ים מִכְרָֽהּ׃
Her husband's heart trusts in her, and he will not lack gain.[^7]
בָּ֣טַח בָּ֭הּ לֵ֣ב בַּעְלָ֑הּ וְ֝שָׁלָ֗ל לֹ֣א יֶחְסָֽר׃
She does him good and not harm all the days of her life.
גְּמָלַ֣תְהוּ ט֣וֹב וְלֹא־רָ֑ע כֹּ֝֗ל יְמֵ֣י חַיֶּֽיה׃
She seeks out wool and flax and works with willing hands.
דָּ֭רְשָׁה צֶ֣מֶר וּפִשְׁתִּ֑ים וַ֝תַּ֗עַשׂ בְּחֵ֣פֶץ כַּפֶּֽיהָ׃
She is like the merchant ships; she brings her food from far away.
הָ֭יְתָה כָּאֳנִיּ֣וֹת סוֹחֵ֑ר מִ֝מֶּרְחָ֗ק תָּבִ֥יא לַחְמָֽהּ׃
She gets up while it is still night and provides food for her household and portions[^8] for her servant girls.
וַתָּ֤קָם ׀ בְּע֬וֹד לַ֗יְלָה וַתִּתֵּ֣ן טֶ֣רֶף לְבֵיתָ֑הּ וְ֝חֹ֗ק לְנַעֲרֹתֶֽיהָ׃
She considers a field and buys it; from her earnings she plants a vineyard.
זָמְמָ֣ה שָׂ֭דֶה וַתִּקָּחֵ֑הוּ מִפְּרִ֥י כַ֝פֶּ֗יהָ *נטע **נָ֣טְעָה כָּֽרֶם׃
She wraps herself in strength and makes her arms strong.[^9]
חָֽגְרָ֣ה בְע֣וֹז מָתְנֶ֑יהָ וַ֝תְּאַמֵּ֗ץ זְרֹעוֹתֶֽיהָ׃
She sees that her trading is profitable; her lamp does not go out at night.
טָ֭עֲמָה כִּי־ט֣וֹב סַחְרָ֑הּ לֹֽא־יִכְבֶּ֖ה *בליל **בַלַּ֣יְלָה נֵרָֽהּ׃
She puts her hands to the distaff, and her palms grasp the spindle.
יָ֭דֶיהָ שִׁלְּחָ֣ה בַכִּישׁ֑וֹר וְ֝כַפֶּ֗יהָ תָּ֣מְכוּ פָֽלֶךְ׃
She opens her hand to the poor and reaches out her hands to the needy.
כַּ֭פָּהּ פָּרְשָׂ֣ה לֶעָנִ֑י וְ֝יָדֶ֗יהָ שִׁלְּחָ֥ה לָֽאֶבְיֽוֹן׃
She is not afraid of the snow for her household, for all her household are clothed in scarlet.[^10]
לֹא־תִירָ֣א לְבֵיתָ֣הּ מִשָּׁ֑לֶג כִּ֥י כָל־בֵּ֝יתָ֗הּ לָבֻ֥שׁ שָׁנִֽים׃
She makes coverings for herself; her clothing is fine linen and purple.
מַרְבַדִּ֥ים עָֽשְׂתָה־לָּ֑הּ שֵׁ֖שׁ וְאַרְגָּמָ֣ן לְבוּשָֽׁהּ׃
Her husband is known at the city gates, when he sits among the elders of the land.
נוֹדָ֣ע בַּשְּׁעָרִ֣ים בַּעְלָ֑הּ בְּ֝שִׁבְתּ֗וֹ עִם־זִקְנֵי־אָֽרֶץ׃
She makes linen garments and sells them, and supplies sashes to the merchants.[^11]
סָדִ֣ין עָ֭שְׂתָה וַתִּמְכֹּ֑ר וַ֝חֲג֗וֹר נָתְנָ֥ה לַֽכְּנַעֲנִֽי׃
Strength and dignity are her clothing, and she laughs at the time to come.
עֹז־וְהָדָ֥ר לְבוּשָׁ֑הּ וַ֝תִּשְׂחַ֗ק לְי֣וֹם אַחֲרֽוֹן׃
She opens her mouth with wisdom, and loving instruction[^12] is on her tongue.
פִּ֭יהָ פָּתְחָ֣ה בְחָכְמָ֑ה וְתֽ[m]וֹרַת חֶ֝֗סֶד עַל־לְשׁוֹנָֽהּ׃
She watches over the ways of her household and does not eat the bread of idleness.
צ֭וֹפִיָּה הֲלִיכ֣וֹת בֵּיתָ֑הּ וְלֶ֥חֶם עַ֝צְל֗וּת לֹ֣א תֹאכֵֽל׃
Her children rise up and call her happy;[^13] her husband too, and he praises her:
קָ֣מוּ בָ֭נֶיהָ וַֽיְאַשְּׁר֑וּהָ בַּ֝עְלָ֗הּ וַֽיְהַֽלְלָהּ׃
"Many women have done capably,[^14] but you surpass them all."
רַבּ֣וֹת בָּ֭נוֹת עָ֣שׂוּ חָ֑יִל וְ֝אַ֗תְּ עָלִ֥ית עַל־כֻּלָּֽנָה׃
Charm is deceptive and beauty is fleeting,[^15] but a woman who fears the LORD[^16] is to be praised.
שֶׁ֣קֶר הַ֭חֵן וְהֶ֣בֶל הַיֹּ֑פִי אִשָּׁ֥ה יִרְאַת־יְ֝הוָ֗ה הִ֣יא תִתְהַלָּֽל׃
Give her the fruit of her hands, and let her works praise her in the gates.
תְּנוּ־לָ֭הּ מִפְּרִ֣י יָדֶ֑יהָ וִֽיהַלְל֖וּהָ בַשְּׁעָרִ֣ים מַעֲשֶֽׂיהָ׃

n.1: Or "The words of Lemuel king of Massa" (see 30:1). Verses 2–9 are the words of his mother.
n.2: The Hebrew word for "son" here is *bar*, the Aramaic word, used three times in this verse.
n.3: The Hebrew text is written "or beer" but read "Where is beer?"
n.4: Literally "all the sons of passing away", perhaps those who are perishing or have no one to stand up for them.
n.5: Hebrew *eshet chayil*, "a woman of strength, of worth", as in 12:4 and Ruth 3:11. Verses 10–31 form an acrostic poem: each verse begins with the next letter of the Hebrew alphabet, from *aleph* to *tav*.
n.6: Hebrew *peninim*, as in 3:15.
n.7: Literally "plunder".
n.8: Or "tasks".
n.9: Literally "She girds her waist with strength".
n.10: With different vowels, "clothed in double garments", as the Vulgate reads.
n.11: Literally "to the Canaanite", a word that came to mean "trader".
n.12: Literally "the instruction (*torah*) of faithful love (*chesed*)". Or "kind teaching".
n.13: The verb is from the same root as *ashrei*, "happy" (see 3:13).
n.14: Hebrew *chayil*, the word translated "capable" in verse 10. Literally "Many daughters have done capably".
n.15: Hebrew *hevel*, "breath, vapor", the word used throughout Ecclesiastes.
n.16: *LORD*: God's personal name, Hebrew YHWH, written "the LORD" in capitals as in most English Bibles.
